title: perf(ui): build the pick overlay lines once per input
body:
Stacked on #2264 (#2248, #2249). Retarget this PR to `main` before #2264 merges.

## What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/pick_line_memo.rs`. `interact::selection_feature_lines` reads the violet pick lines from it. One miss runs the old build (`feature_lines`) one time. A hit returns the shared `Arc<[[f32; 6]]>`.
- The key is the input itself (rule 2 of `docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`), never `doc_version`:
  - the shown pick list, by value;
  - the pick ink;
  - the vertex cross arm, only when a vertex is picked;
  - for each picked model: the display-off flag, the entity, the `Arc<Features>` allocation and the view pose.
- `pick_line_builds()` counts the real builds. `selection_feature_lines_fresh` (test only) builds without the memo.
- The probe `frame_cost_probe` collects the scene one time before its window. The shell does this on the first frame of an input; the harness does not. The probe asserts `pick_lines` = 0 on still frames.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2250-pick-overlay-lines.md`.

## Safety

The lines are display only. No generator, check or post reads them. No cut geometry, chain or golden changed.

## Readings (release, fig8, `frame_cost_probe::still`, ms per still frame, whole stack #2254, #2255, #2259, #2264, #2266)

| State | Before (#2238) | After | `selection_features` after |
|---|---|---|---|
| a nothing selected | 3.5 | 3.8 | 0.012 |
| b contour, top chains | 13.1 | 5.1 | 0.013 |
| c 2D Adaptive, welded face, preview | 30.0 | 6.0 | 0.012 (was 1.48) |
| d toolpath shown | 3.3 | 3.6 | 0.002 |
| e simulation paused | 3.4 | 4.1 | 0.003 |

The a, d and e values are in the run-to-run noise. The largest remaining piece is `ui/viewport.pick_ink` in state c (0.91 ms). It is not in the scope of #2250.

Test build (not launched): `.claude/tmp/test-builds/camcraft-framecost-fd68dfd90.exe`.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_caches::pick_lines_build_once_per_input`. Still frames build nothing. Each answer equals a fresh build after: a new pick, a hidden model, a move of fig8, and each undo.
- `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`: `pick_lines` = 0 in states a-e.

## Gate

- `camcraft-ui` lib: 972 passed, 6 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `main` is red in `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs` (E0063: missing fields `stepdown` and `stepover` in `CuttingRow`). This PR does not touch `camcraft-app`.

## Not exercised

- A theme change and a change of the active setup with picks shown (the key holds the ink and the view pose, but no test changes them).
- The setup-page drafts (plane, points, axis, locate) through the memo. They use the same function and the same key.

Changelog: Performance: the viewport no longer outlines the picked faces and edges again on each frame.

Effort: medium (no escalation).

Fixes #2250

title: perf(app): walk the selection once per input for the page
body:
Stacked on #2259 (#2247). Retarget this PR to `main` before #2259 merges.

## What changed

- New `crates/app/src/operation/selection_memo.rs`. It keeps the answers of the selection walk for the display: the account notes, the door refusal and the Contour Auto side.
- The key is the input itself (rule 2 of `docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`), never `doc_version`:
  - the setup, the picks and the parameters, by value;
  - for each picked entity and the setup's stock: the entity, the `Facets` allocation, the `Location`, and the setup alignment flag;
  - for the setup: the effective setup, the `SetupDef`, the machine kind, the WCS pose and word;
  - the document unit.
- `operation::selection_account` (Geometry tab) and `operation::contour_auto_side` (Contour fields) read the memo. The two share one entry, so one walk serves the two.
- `selection_walks()` counts the real walks. `contour_auto_side_fresh` and `selection_account_fresh` walk without the memo, for the pins.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2248-selection-walk.md`.

## Safety (rule 6)

Generation reads the side from its own walk in `job` (`selection_geometry_impl`). The pick doors (`selection_refusal`) and the region walk (`selection_geometry`) also walk for themselves. The generator and the post do not read this memo. The side that the toolpath uses does not change. No cut geometry, chain or golden changed.

## Readings

Release, fig8, state b (#2238 probe), before: `selection_account` 4.24-4.48 ms and `contour_auto_side` 4.13-4.45 ms on each still frame. After: 0 walks on a still frame (debug probe count). The release table for the full stack goes on #2238 after the last piece (#2250).

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_caches::contour_side_and_account_walk_once_per_input`. Each answer equals a fresh walk. The test changes each input: each top chain alone, undo, all chains again, side Inside through `EditOperationParams` and undo, `MoveModel` of fig8 and undo.
- `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`: `selections` = 0 in states a-e.

## Gate

- `camcraft-app` lib (356 passed) and tests `area_controls area_open blind_slot circular_pick face_holes open_band operations opframe_picks pick_doors probe_pick project_roundtrip shoulder_adaptive slot_caps slot_picks solid_law_goldens stitch_cross tilt units_in_refusals`: all pass.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: 971 passed, 6 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test pick_doors --test operations -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `main` is red in `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs` (E0063: missing fields `stepdown` and `stepover` in `CuttingRow`). This is not from this PR, so `--all-targets` for `camcraft-app` was not run.

## Not exercised

- A change of the stock entity or of the setup alignment and WCS tilt with an open page (the key holds them, but no test changes them).
- Facing and pocket kinds through the memo (the pins use a Contour).

Changelog: Performance: the Geometry tab and the Contour fields no longer walk the selection again on each frame.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Fixes #2248

body:
## Cause

The post-merge batch gate failed in step 1, `debug build (--no-run)` (runs 43935486746 and 43935744100). The cause is in test code only. Product code builds.

1. PR #2140 (EDM wire tool) added two tests with a `CuttingRow` literal of the old shape. PR #2101 (it includes #2015) made `material` an `Option<WorkMaterial>` and added `stepdown` and `stepover`. Each PR built alone. After the two merges, these targets do not compile:
   - `crates/tools/src/wire.rs:103` (lib test of `camcraft-tools`)
   - `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs:106` (test `wire_tool` of `camcraft-app`)
2. After the build is fixed, a test fails. PR #2215 added `testdata/models/fig8.step` without a row in the STEP agreement bench. `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` fails with `a fixture has no row, or a row has no fixture - re-triage`.

The xtask gate change of #1952 is not the cause.

## What changed

- The two wire tests build the row with `CuttingRow::plain(Some(WorkMaterial::MildSteel), 0.0, <feed>)`. Each test keeps its "EDM conditions" refusal assertion.
- `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs` has a row for `fig8.step` and the per-file test `step_fig8`. The row pins the reading that the bench gives: `solidcore refuses: #14 at read: pcurves failed on`, `no exact solid to judge against`. This is the same class as `fillet_corner.step`.

No safety check or refusal is removed.

## Readings and tests

- The batch build step `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run`: exit 0 on Windows.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --failed gate-logs/quick-20261116-193211` on the final head: `kernel suites: step_agreement` ok (19 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test wire_tool`: 5 passed. `camcraft-tools --lib wire`: 1 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test wire_tool -- -D warnings`: clean.

Pinned by: `wire_tool_command_refuses_bad_rpm_diameter_corner_and_cutting_rows_by_name`, the `wire` lib test of `camcraft-tools`, `step_fig8`, `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name`.

- The Linux runner. The build and the tests ran on Windows only.
- The ui suites and clippy of the full batch tier. The post-merge gate runs them after the merge.

title: fix(mcp): batch AI undo, add get_selection, and enforce live confirmation gate
body:
## Before/after screenshots

Real 1280×720 egui shell renders with offline `ScriptedTransport`. Images live only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch at `775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1`.

| Behavior | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One Ctrl+Z after a three-command AI turn | ![Stock and tool remain after undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/before-one-ctrl-z.png) | ![All three turn edits removed after undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/after-one-ctrl-z.png) |
| Native-mode machine edit | ![Machine loads without confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/before-machine-confirmation.png) | ![Machine edit waits for Allow or Deny](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/after-machine-confirmation.png) |

The before renders reproduce the prior behavior with temporary reversions: disable history-group folding for undo; restore the former Native confirmation allowlist and bypass the newly added live gate for `load_machine` for machine loading. The after renders use the current PR behavior. All capture edits were restored; no screenshots or capture code were added to this PR branch.

Existing pins were mutation-checked again: `one_ctrl_z_reverts_multi_call_ai_chat_turn` and `machine_and_limit_edits_require_confirmation_and_unapproved_live_dispatch_blocks` both failed with their behavior reverted and passed after restoration.

## What changed
- Added `BatchCommand` and stackable `History::begin_group` / `commit_group` / `cancel_group` in `crates/app/src/commands/batch.rs` and `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`.
- Wired `State::submit_ai_prompt`, `State::run`, `AiChatState::poll`, and `ChatTurn::finish` so a contiguous multi-call AI turn commits as one `BatchCommand` undo step (`Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y`).
- Added the read-only `get_selection` MCP tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/selection.rs`) and `SelectionContext` snapshot (`State::selection_context`) so live sessions report selected entities, active setup, selected/active operation, viewport `pick_mode`, and `geometry_picks` without breaking `ui -> app` layering.
- Added `LiveGate`, `GateKind`, `ApprovedCall`, `requires_approval`, `LiveOptions`, and `answer_live_with` in `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`; `answer_live` now fails closed via `&LiveOptions::default()`.
- Updated `AiChatState`, `transport::requires_confirmation`, `worker`, and `mcp_host::pump` to share `requires_approval` and `is_read_only_tool`, bind `Allow` clicks to one `ApprovedCall`, and never auto-approve `post`, `load_machine`, or `edit_machine`.
- Updated `undo_turn_reverts_multi_tool_turn_changes_in_one_click_and_guards_later_edits` (`#2094`) from `pre_depth + 3` to `pre_depth + 1` to reflect the collapsed `BatchCommand` entry.
- Recorded design decisions in `docs/decisions/1942-ai-chat-safety.md`.

## Cause
Before this fix, AI chat turns pushed one `History` entry per tool call (requiring multiple `Ctrl+Z` presses), `get_selection` did not exist for AI inspection of viewport picks, `FallbackMode::Native` skipped confirmation for machine and limit tools, and `answer_live` lacked a server-side permission gate.

## Tests
Pinning tests (all red on unchanged `upstream/main` `e808c9629`, green after fix):
- `camcraft-app --test batch_undo`: `begin_and_commit_group_folds_multi_command_turn_into_one_undo_step`, `empty_and_nested_groups_and_direct_batch_command_behave_cleanly`, `cancel_group_keeps_existing_commands_separate` (3 passed, 0 failed).
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_live`: `get_selection_returns_selected_entities_and_empty_picks_headless`, `live_permission_gate_blocks_unapproved_post_file_writes_paths_and_machine_limits`, `get_selection_reads_live_ui_selection_context_and_prompt_json_treats_it_read_only`, `live_gate_allows_explicitly_approved_calls_and_never_auto_approves_post_or_machine_edits` (14 passed, 0 failed in `mcp_live`; `mcp`: 22 passed; `mcp_provider`: 9 passed).
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: `one_ctrl_z_reverts_multi_call_ai_chat_turn`, `get_selection_mcp_tool_reads_ui_geo_picks_pick_mode_and_selected_entities`, `machine_and_limit_edits_require_confirmation_and_unapproved_live_dispatch_blocks`, plus updated #2094 `undo_turn_reverts_multi_tool_turn_changes_in_one_click_and_guards_later_edits` (`camcraft-ui --lib`: 968 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored).

Mutation checks (all 5 confirmed red when reverted, green when restored):
1. Bypass `LiveGate::check` (`Ok(())`): `live_permission_gate_blocks_unapproved_post_file_writes_paths_and_machine_limits` failed (wrote `blocked.nc`), restored -> passed.
2. Bypass `GateKind::allows_auto_approve` (`true`): `live_gate_allows_explicitly_approved_calls_and_never_auto_approves_post_or_machine_edits` failed (`post` auto-approved), restored -> passed.
3. Revert `transport::requires_confirmation` `Native` arm to the old 6-tool list: `machine_and_limit_edits_require_confirmation_and_unapproved_live_dispatch_blocks` failed (timed out waiting for confirmation), restored -> passed.
4. Make `History::commit_group` return `false` without batching: `begin_and_commit_group_folds_multi_command_turn_into_one_undo_step` and `one_ctrl_z_reverts_multi_call_ai_chat_turn` failed, restored -> passed.
5. Pass `selection: None` in `mcp_host::answer_request`: `get_selection_mcp_tool_reads_ui_geo_picks_pick_mode_and_selected_entities` failed (`pick_mode` null), restored -> passed.

Gate and clippy:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 271 of 273 steps passed (`app:lib` 355 passed / 1 ignored, 254 `app` suites, `ui:lib` 968 passed / 6 ignored, 14 `ui` suites); only `app build (--no-run)` and `app suites: wire_tool` failed to compile due to pre-existing `upstream/main` issue `#2244` (`crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs:106` `CuttingRow` literal mismatch).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` hit the same `#2244` compile error in `wire_tool.rs`; targeting `camcraft-app` (`--lib --bins --test batch_undo --test mcp_live --test mcp --test mcp_provider`) and `camcraft-ui --all-targets` passed with `-D warnings`.

## Goldens moved
None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised
- Interactive live HTTPS calls to an external LLM API endpoint (tested via `ScriptedTransport` and live JSON-RPC loopback `Request::pair` dispatch).
- Pre-existing broken binary `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs` (`#2244` on `upstream/main`).
- Full `gate batch` and `gate release` suites (only `gate quick` ran per issue-worker rules).

## Overlaps
Touches the same files (different functions/items; whichever merges second refreshes): `#2259`, `#2256`, `#2254`, `#2253`, `#2197`, `#2187`, `#2185`, `#2150`, `#2149`, `#2134`, `#2122` (`needs-maintainer`), `#2100`, `#2092`, `#2077`, `#1798`, `#1738`, `#1330`.

Branched from `upstream/main` (`e808c9629`).
Effort: high
Changelog: AI chat turns now undo in one grouped Ctrl+Z step, expose read-only `get_selection`, and enforce live confirmation gating.
Fixes #1942

title: perf(ui): group welded faces once per feature set for the pick chips
body:
Stacked on #2255. The base is `issue/2246-area-preview-fill`. Retarget this PR to `main` before #2255 merges.

## What changed

- New `crates/app/src/model/patch_memo.rs`: `model::patches` and `model::patch_rings` memoize `feature::patches` and `feature::patch_rings`. The key is the allocation of the `Arc<Features>`, the same key as `model::resolve_chain` (#2235). A landing makes a new allocation, so it is a new key. The counter is `model::patch_builds`.
- `State::geo_chips` (welded-face chip label) and `pick::face_origin` read the memo. `face_origin` is used by the chips and by `pick::align_321`.
- `face_origin` finds the strips of a patch with a binary search in the sorted `Patch::faces`. Before, it did a linear `contains` for each face of the model.
- `docs/decisions/2247-pick-chip-patches.md`.

The answers are the same as a fresh grouping. No change to commands, picks, the WCS result, cut geometry or posted G-code.

## Readings (fig8, state c of the #2238 probe, ms for each still frame)

| Piece | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `ui/properties.op.picks.chips` (release) | 4.68 | see the stack table in #2238 |
| `ui/properties.op.picks.align_321` (release) | 1.98 | see the stack table in #2238 |
| `ui/properties.op.picks.chips` (debug) | 12.29 | 0.78 |
| `ui/properties.op.picks.align_321` (debug) | 11.73 | 0.31 |

## Tests

- `model::patch_memo::tests::a_hit_answers_what_a_fresh_grouping_answers_and_groups_once` (app): a hit equals `feature::patches` and `feature::patch_rings`; a miss is kept; a new allocation groups again.
- `frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`: the patch counter is 0 on a still frame in states a to e.
- `frame_cost_caches::pick_chips_group_the_welded_faces_once_and_follow_the_picks` (new): the memo equals a fresh grouping on fig8; still frames group nothing; a new pick gives a new chip list; the undo gives the first chips and the first 3-2-1 answer.
- `camcraft-app` tests `face_origin`, `plane_align`, `pick_agnostic`, `feature`, `orient_dropdowns`: pass.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: 970 passed, 6 ignored.
- Clippy `-D warnings`: `camcraft-ui --all-targets` clean; `camcraft-app --lib` and the tests above clean. `camcraft-app --all-targets` does not build on `main`: `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs` (not touched here).

## Not exercised

- The other `feature::patches` callers (commands, MCP, heights) do not use the memo. They do not run on each frame.
- The real window.

Changelog: The operation page with a welded-face pick no longer slows the viewport: the face grouping is computed once for each model.
Effort: high

Fixes #2247

body:
## What changed

Property-row checkboxes use their visible captions as accessible names.
The structural twin checks the `Repeat each depth` checkbox on the Threading Passes tab.
It checks the label, checkbox role, enabled state and keyboard activation.
The existing `Climb milling` caption-click test selects the caption by role to preserve its original click target.

## Cause

The shared form helper drew a separate caption and an unnamed checkbox.
The checkbox's empty direct AccessKit label also hid an associated caption.

## Tests

- `thread_passes_repeat_each_depth_checkbox_has_label_role_and_enabled_state` failed on unchanged upstream/main `e808c9629` and passes with the fix.
- Restoring the complete upstream helper makes the pin fail. Restoring the fix makes it pass.
- Removing only `labelled_by` makes the pin fail. Restoring it makes the pin pass.
- Removing only `clear_label` makes the pin fail. Restoring it makes the pin pass.
- `click_apply_edits_operation_through_commands` passes with the explicit caption target.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes. The UI library reports 966 passed and 6 ignored. All six selected integration suites pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

## Goldens moved

None. The diff contains no NC or CL golden changes. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

No manual GUI or screen-reader check ran.
The new structural pin checks keyboard activation of the named checkbox.
It does not check a mouse click on the right-column square.
A trial with generic `get_by_label("Climb milling")` selected the newly named right-column square.
That click did not toggle the staged value, including after five frames for the scroll to settle.
The role-specific caption query preserves the original click path, and that test passes.
This fix does not change the pointer layout or toggle implementation.

## Overlaps

PRs #2090, #2068, #1996, #1798, #1717 and #1687 touch `structural.rs` in other functions or module registrations.
PRs #2254, #2253, #2197, #2185, #2149, #2146, #2096, #2092, #2090, #2078, #2077, #2068, #1996, #1931, #1330 and #1209 touch `tests.rs` in other functions.

Changelog: Property-row checkboxes expose their captions to accessibility tools, with structural coverage for Repeat each depth.

title: fix(ui): cache pick highlight geometry and batch stroke draws
body:
## What changed

- Added thread-local weak lookup indexes (`resolve_chain_arc`, `patches_arc`, `patch_rings_arc`) in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/index.rs`.
- Removed per-triangle heap allocations in `digest_of` and hoisted lattice construction in `patches` and `patch_rings` inside `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`.

title: feat(post): add G93 inverse-time feed solver and section mode markers
body:
## What changed
- Added `crates/post/src/post/g93.rs` implementing the shared Rust `G93` inverse-time feed solver (`F = 1 / dt_min`, `min^-1`).
- Computed `dt_cut = ||tip_1 - tip_0|| / v_prog` in part space, computed `dt_lim` from stated linear (`X/Y/Z` `mm/min`) and rotary (`A/B/C` `deg/min`) `max_normal_speed` limits, and took `dt_min = max(dt_cut, dt_lim)`.
- Handled pure rotary reorientations (`ds_tip <= eps`) using configured `rotary_only_deg_per_min`, stated axis limits, or `v_prog` fallback without division by zero, and skipped zero-motion duplicate moves (`G93Decision::Skip`).
- Clamped finite `F` to `f_min..=f_max` (`0.001..=60_000.0`), floor-formatted `F` words to 4 decimals (`format_g93_feed_word`), refused invalid feeds, limits, or options by name, and verified `G20` (inch) vs `G21` (mm) unit invariance.
- Re-exported `g93` APIs from `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs`, `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs`, and `crates/post/src/kinematics/mod.rs`.

title: fix(ui): compute a chain selection's geometry once, not on each frame
body:
## What changed

A still frame with chains in the open operation's selection took 0.4-1.6 s. Each frame did three costly things again:

- `model::features_of` content-hashed all the facets of the model.
- `feature::resolve_chain` walked all the model's chains (about 5 ms) for each chain and for each caller (chips, stitch, account, region, refusal, overlay).
- `pocket_region_on_part` sliced the part at each ladder plane (about 15 ms), for each of three `region_of` calls.

This PR adds three caches of derived values and one per-scene memo. No cache is a command. No cache is in the project file. Each key is the input itself, so a stale answer cannot occur:

1. `model::features_of_shared` (app): the features of one model, keyed by the allocation of its facet `Arc`. A landing (`set_facets`) makes a new allocation, thus a new key.
2. `model::resolve_chain` (app, new `model/chain_memo.rs`): the chain for one `ChainId`, keyed by the allocation of the `Arc<Features>`.
3. `operation::pocket_memo` (app, new file): the pocket family's region on a part, keyed by the exact input (loops, part facets, planes, unit). The region and the `Invalid` / `Empty` refusals are kept.
4. `frame_memo::scene_scope` (ui, new file): one `region_of` for each operation in one `world::collect`. The memo is dropped at the end of the scope.

The change of `feature::resolve_chain(` to `model::resolve_chain(` in about 15 files is a signature ripple, not new logic. The pick result, the stitch result and all cut geometry are the same. The hover path and the highlighter (#2201) are not changed.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2235-selection-frame-cost.md` (it quotes the maintainer).

## Readings (headless, release, fig8.step, 8-10 chains on the top edge)

| Stage | Scene collect | UI step |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 640-765 ms | 425-510 ms |
| After the features and chain memos | 48-50 ms | 18-19 ms |
| After the pocket memo | 9.5 ms | 6 ms |
| After the per-scene memo | 5.8-6.4 ms | 5.1-5.7 ms |

One real frame is about 6 ms headless. Of that, `region_of` is about 1.6 ms (the ladder's facet copies in `material_of`). The rest is egui layout and the overlay. A still frame makes no feature digest, no chain walk and no part slice.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::selection_frame_cost::frames_without_a_change_walk_digest_and_slice_nothing` (ui): 10 still frames add no chain walk, digest or slice, and exactly one region build per scene.
- `egui_app::tests::selection_frame_cost::a_selection_change_or_a_landing_is_a_new_answer` (ui): a new selection walks and slices again and the region follows it; a landing takes a new digest and walk; the drawn region equals the fresh compute.
- `operation::pocket_memo::law::a_hit_is_the_fresh_answer_and_any_changed_input_slices_again` (app lib)
- `model::chain_memo::tests::a_hit_answers_what_a_fresh_walk_answers_and_walks_once` (app lib)

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick` selects all suites, because origin/main is 36 commits ahead of the branch base. So I ran the touched binaries instead:

- `camcraft-app --lib` (354 pass) and 35 app test binaries: area_chains, area_picks, area_open, area_controls, pocket_recognition, rest_pocket, whole_model_pocket, pocket_overhead, slot_picks, slot_pick_refusals, feature, feature_pick, pick, pick_doors, heights_selection, stitch_cross, probe_pick, golden_cl, posting, recorded_post_streams, solid_law_goldens, opframe_picks, box_pick, circle_centre, circular_pick, centre_pick, contour_open_side, contour_auto_level, mcp_pick, mcp_pockets, commands_undo, wire_contour, align_axes, points_align, plane_align_edges. All pass.
- `camcraft-ui` full suite (lib 956 pass, 6 ignored, and all ui test binaries). All pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Goldens (`golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`) did not move.

## Not exercised

- The GPU frame time in the real app. The readings are headless. A release test build is for the maintainer.
- The hover path (#2201) is not measured or changed.
- The heavy release lanes and the pixel snapshots.
- `selection.rs`, `interact.rs` and `model.rs` were over 400 lines before this PR. This PR adds one or two lines to each and does not split them.

Changelog: The viewport stays fast with chains in an operation's geometry selection: the selection's chains and pocket region are computed once when the selection or the model changes, not on each frame.

Effort: high

Fixes #2235

title: fix(tools): a refused tool names itself and the rule it breaks
body:
#1186: the project loader refused a tool with bad numbers. The message was `tool parameters are not usable: ToolDto { ... }`, with the full structure. The refusal was correct, but it did not name the tool or the field. `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` printed a similar dump. The library import and the library reader gave a general message.

The branch has upstream main at a529c455, merged in.

## What changed

- **`Tool::why_not_sane() -> Option<String>`** (new file `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`). It gives the first rule that a tool breaks, in plain words. Examples:
  - `turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min (it must be over 0)`
  - `corner radius 100 mm is more than half the 6 mm diameter`
  - `a drill's tip angle 50 degrees must be over 60`
  - `a sinker electrode turns no spindle: its spindle speed must be 0, not 1000 rpm`
  - `TurningData::why_not_sane` gives the same for the turning limits.
- **One source of truth.** `Tool::is_sane` and `TurningData::is_sane` are now `why_not_sane().is_none()`. Thus the message and the verdict cannot be different. The rules moved out of `tools.rs` in the same order, with the same limits.
- **The rules that main added are included.** Main added these after the branch started:
  - the `pitch_min` field;
  - the waterjet, electrode and thread-mill kinds and their rules;
  - the catalog and cutting-row refusals.
  - Each of these rules has its own message now.
- **Four refusals now read `tool '<name>': <rule>`:**
  - the project loader (`project/validate.rs`), which is the case in the issue;
  - `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` (`commands/tool.rs`);
  - the tool-library import (`commands/tool_import.rs`);
  - the library reader (`tool_library.rs`).
  - The MCP tools `add_tool` and `edit_tool` use the same commands. Thus an agent also gets the named rule.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1186-tool-refusal-names.md`.

## Tests

New pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/project_tool_refusal.rs` opens a saved file with one bad field through the real loader (`project::open`).
  - `a_bad_turning_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: surface speed 0, a negative feed per rev, and a max rpm below the rpm of the tool.
  - `a_bad_milling_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: a corner radius more than half the diameter, and feed 0.
  - The two tests also make sure that the message has no `ToolDto` dump.
- `tools::tool_sanity::tests`:
  - `a_turning_field_is_named`, `a_milling_field_is_named` and `the_newer_kinds_are_named`.
  - `the_named_law_gives_the_old_verdict_everywhere` keeps the `is_sane` body of main as an oracle. It also keeps the `TurningData::is_sane` body.
  - The test examines each catalog tool as each of the 17 kinds. It sets each of the 14 numeric fields to 13 edge values: 0, negative, the 60 and 180 degree limits, more than 500, NaN and infinity. It also examines flute counts, orientation codes and turning data.
  - The new law gives the same verdict in all cases. Thus no tool changes from accepted to refused, or from refused to accepted.

Changed test: `tool_cutter_params::a_reshape_is_refused_by_name_against_the_new_numbers` looked for the old text "finite and positive". It now looks for `tool '<name>': diameter -1 mm is outside`.

Gates on dbf7799e:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green.
  - The tools step ran the lib tests and `waterjet`.
  - The app step ran the lib tests and 44 suites. These include all `tool_*` suites, `project_tool_refusal`, `project_roundtrip`, `thread_mill`, `waterjet_machine`, `plasma_profile`, `mcp` and `commands_undo`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- The UI shows these refusals in the status line, as before. No UI test reads their text. A search of `crates/ui` finds none of the old messages.
- A missing or unknown field is a serde parse error. It occurs before this law runs. The serde message already names the field, and it does not change.

Changelog: A tool refused for unusable numbers (project load, add or edit tool, library import) now names the tool and the rule it breaks, e.g. "tool 'T1': turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min", instead of printing the whole definition (#1186)

Effort: low (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #1186

title: fix(geometry): one smooth crease between curved faces is one feature edge
body:
## What changed

- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/g1_seam.rs` (new): the G1 seam rule of `feature::chains`. Two feature edges join at a vertex when all of these are true:
  - the two edges separate the same two welded patches, or both are the rim of one open sheet;
  - the vertex has no other real feature edge (a tessellation seam inside one patch does not count);
  - the turn is at most `CHAIN_TANGENT_DEG` (30 degrees).
- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/trail.rs` (new): the trail walk, moved out of `feature.rs`. It keeps a joined pair consecutive in one trail. With no seam pair in a component, the walk is the same as before.
- `feature.rs` shrinks by 6 lines. It is still over the 400-line limit, as on `main`.
- `testdata/models/fig8.step`: new fixture from the maintainer's model.
- `docs/decisions/2209-join-g1-edges.md`: the angle limit, the layer, and the dropped options.

Root cause: `fig8.step` has 70 `EDGE_CURVE` entities, so the file does not store short edges. The face rule joins two edges only when they bound one planar face. On a crease between a cone and a cylinder, no two chords share a planar face, so each chord was one chain.

## Readings (fig8.step)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pickable edges | 2162 | 2162 |
| chains | 1593 | 877 |
| runs of the edge below the chamfer (z 19) | 719, longest 17.22 mm | 10, longest 188.49 mm |
| runs of the edge above the chamfer (z 20) | 10, longest 194.77 mm | 10, longest 194.77 mm |

Over all STEP fixtures in `testdata/models`, the tangent pieces at a two-edge vertex were: fig8 719 and spline_revolved 59 before. After the fix, the count is 0 in each fixture.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/feature_edge_g1_join.rs`:
- `fig8_edge_below_the_chamfer_picks_whole_like_the_edge_above`
- `no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`
- `a_smooth_crease_cut_into_chords_chains_as_one_edge`
- `a_sharp_corner_on_the_same_crease_still_splits`
- `a_degenerate_band_never_panics`

Gate (debug, `-j 6`): all `camcraft-geometry` suites pass. These `camcraft-app` suites pass: `feature`, `feature_pick`, `feature_pick_wire`, `feature_edge_g1_join`, `pick`, `pick_agnostic`, `area_chains`, `area_picks`, `area_open`, `box_pick`, `golden_cl`, `slot_picks`, `opframe_picks`, `contour_start_point`, `heights_selection`, `project_roundtrip`, `mcp_pick`, `plane_align_edges`, `vertex_pick`, `circular_pick`, `regression_models`, `deburr_links`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Saved selections and goldens

- No golden `.cl` or `.nc` file changed. `golden_cl` passes without an update.
- A saved chain selection that holds the id of one old piece still resolves. `feature::resolve_chain` falls back from chain to run to the single edge id. The old id is the id of that one chord, so it resolves to the same chord. It never resolves to a different edge.
- A chain that now holds more chords gets a new chain id. A new pick of that edge selects the full edge.

## Not exercised

- The full quick gate (it runs all downstream suites of `camcraft-geometry`). Only the suites above ran.
- The ui suites, and the GUI by hand. A release build is given to the maintainer for a hand test.
- Frame time while an edge is selected (#2201). It was not measured.

Changelog: An edge between two curved faces (for example below a chamfer on a round wall) now picks as one full edge, not as many short pieces.

Effort: high

Fixes #2209

title: fix(setup): resolve 2D area controls in an aligned setup
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`: `generation_problem` no longer refuses area controls in an aligned setup. The refusal applied to the four verified 2D kinds: Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive. One change fixes all four.
- The area law already reads each world value in the setup frame: the picked faces and edges (`selection_geometry_in`), the stitched open chains, the part material and its silhouette (`setup_align::facets_in`) and the heights. The stock outline is furniture and stays unaligned, as in #326. Thus no second transform is added. A second transform would turn the picks two times.
- The tilt refusal and the refusal of the unverified kinds stay.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2210-aligned-area-controls.md`.

## Readings and pinning tests

New file `crates/app/tests/setup_align_2d_area.rs`. The part is an L with unequal arms. Setup1 turns it 90 degrees about Z (`AlignPreset::TurnZ90`). The turned L, the L as modelled and the L turned -90 degrees are three different regions. Each case generates in the aligned document and in a document with the turn baked into the mesh. Each case asserts:
- the two paths agree to 1e-6 mm, and the two posted programs are equal;
- no warning blocks the post, the program stock simulation finds 0 gouge cells, and the setup posts.

Cases:
- `turned_adaptive2d_excludes_the_picked_face_where_the_part_lies` and `turned_pocket2d_excludes_the_picked_face_where_the_part_lies`: an exclude boundary of the picked top face. The feed passes (sampled each 0.25 mm) stay a tool radius off the turned L. They reach (8, 15), which is inside the modelled L and inside the -90 L.
- `turned_face_clears_the_band_of_the_turned_pick`: Face refuses an exclude boundary by its own law, so the case uses a 1 mm offset. The band reaches Y 23 and stays in X [4 - r, 26 + r].
- `turned_contour2d_offset_rides_the_turned_outline`: the ride stays r + 1 off the turned L and passes beside the turned long arm at X 28.
- `as_modelled_area_controls_never_meet_the_aligned_door`: an unaligned setup gets no refusal.

Updated: `opframe_picks::tilt_times_picks_and_unverified_stay_refused_and_area_passes_in_phase_two`, `setup_align_3d::enabling_aligned_3d_keeps_tilt_refused_and_passes_2d_area`.

Gate: these suites pass in debug: `setup_align_2d_area`, `opframe_picks`, `setup_align_3d`, `setup_align`, `area_controls`, `area_open`, `area_picks`, `area_chains`, `area_overhead`, `open_band`, `opframe_seam`, `align_axes`, `align_compose`, `plane_align`, `points_align`, `winding_align`, and the `camcraft-app` lib tests. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The full quick gate selected all suites for this diff; I did not run that full set.

## Posted G-code and goldens

An unaligned setup does not change: `generation_problem` returns early when the setup has no alignment, and no generator code changed. No golden file changes. An aligned setup with area controls now posts where it was refused before.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real control.
- The fig8 reproduction from the issue was not generated in the GUI by me. A release build of this head is given to the maintainer for that check.
- `boundary_picks::extend_to_loop` (a UI helper that picks the most horizontal face) reads face normals without the setup frame. For a turn about Z the result is the same. For a flip or a free angle it can select a different face. It only seeds a selection and does not cut. This is not changed here.
- Tilted planes and the unverified kinds stay refused.

Changelog: 2D Adaptive, 2D Pocket, 2D Contour and Face now accept area controls (boundaries, offset, containment) in a setup that holds the part turned; before, generation refused them.

Effort: high

Fixes #2210

title: fix(3d): keep masked 3D Pocket clear to open edges
body:
## What changed
- Extracted `mask_center` in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs` and added `MASK_RESIDUE = 1.0`.
- `ladder` now erodes the unmasked `target` by `r + stock_to_leave` first so only model islands act as walls.
- `mask_center` intersects `mask.above(z)` with `center.offset(r)` (the swept envelope of `center`) instead of raw `target`.
- `mask_center` opens the standing region by `MASK_RESIDUE * mask.cell()` using mitered offsets (`offset_sharp`) to drop one-cell lattice residue on walls without rounding grid corners.
- `mask_center` then intersects `center` with `standing.offset(r)` so only centers whose disc meets standing stock remain.
- Added `masked_empty` tracking in `ladder` so levels emptied by the mask report nothing left to cut instead of "too narrow".
- Added `crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs` and `docs/decisions/1749-mask-edge.md`.

## Cause
In `sc_logo.camproj`, `S1 Adaptive rough profile` cleared the stock just outside the part silhouette before `S1 Notch adaptive + terrace finish` ran. The re-machining mask boundary sat on the part edge. Because `ladder` intersected `target` with the mask before eroding by the tool radius, the mask boundary acted as a wall one radius thick and left standing stock at the notch open edges where Setup 2 `Soft jaw (9)` stands. Using `target` instead of `center.offset(r)` in `mask_center` also caused a redundant duplicate op with positive `stock_to_leave` to re-cut corner slivers instead of refusing.

## Tests
- Pins (`crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs`):
  - `a_masked_pocket_still_clears_the_open_edge_beside_a_wall` — ok
  - `the_mask_still_keeps_the_cutter_off_cleared_ground` — ok
  - `filleted_notch_after_outside_profile_clears_open_edge_corner_for_jaws` — ok (100 levels at `stepdown = 0.15`, `shell = true`, R3.125 fillets, 0.254 mm outside-profile mask)
  - `a_redundant_duplicate_with_stock_to_leave_refuses` — ok
- Gate and clippy after final edit:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed (`wall 15.9 min, 2 step(s), 0 failed`).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed (0 warnings).
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_open_side --test remachining --test whole_model_pocket`: `pocket3d_open_side` 7 passed; `remachining` 6 passed; `whole_model_pocket` 5 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane).
- Mutations:
  1. Reverted `ladder.rs` to `upstream/main`: `pocket3d_mask_edge` failed 3 of 4 (`a_masked_pocket_still_clears_the_open_edge_beside_a_wall` left Z 1.000 over `(0.050, 19.950)`; `filleted_notch_after_outside_profile_clears_open_edge_corner_for_jaws` left Z 34.826 over `(0.050, 13.184)`; `a_redundant_duplicate_with_stock_to_leave_refuses` refused the smaller finish collar). Restored: 4 passed.
  2. Set `MASK_RESIDUE = 0.0`: `remachining::a_redundant_duplicate_refuses_rather_than_cutting_air` failed. Restored: `remachining` 6 passed.
  3. Intersected mask with `&target` instead of `center.offset(r)` in `mask_center`: `a_redundant_duplicate_with_stock_to_leave_refuses` failed. Restored: 4 passed.

## Goldens moved
None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised
- Running `camcraft-cli` directly on the private `~/sc-parts/sc_logo.camproj` file was blocked by the headless command allowlist (`permission check failed for unsandboxed ".../target/release/camcraft-cli"`). That project also hits the separate `HolderProfile::enclose` shank-widening issue (`#2199` / PR `#2179`) on `T31 1/4 3FL`.
- Full `xtask gate batch` and `xtask gate release` suites did not run here (`xtask gate quick` and the listed `camcraft-app` suites ran).

## Overlaps
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`: **#2149** (`feat(boundaries)!`, already stacked on `#2077`, `conflicts`) and **#2035** (`feat(motion)`, incomplete draft, `conflicts`) also modify `pub(super) fn ladder` on non-overlapping lines (`avoid` keep-outs / `stock` arg vs `mask_center` / `standing`). Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: 3D Pocket and Multi-Axis Rough: a re-machining mask no longer creates a false wall along open notch edges after an outside profile cut, and ignores unreachable corners and wall stock-to-leave collars.

Fixes #1749

title: fix(sim): judge the stated shank below a holder foot drawn beside it
body:
## What changed

- Added strict interior `span_reach` to `HolderProfile` in `crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs` and switched `enclose` to it. A holder band starting at `shank_top` (like the #2180 cone) no longer widens `shank_d`, while a band strictly inside `(flute_len, shank_top)` still widens `enclose`'s single-cylinder fallback for single-cylinder callers.
- Added `camcraft_tools::neck::shank_with_body` in `crates/tools/src/neck.rs`. When a holder band reaches inside `(flute_len, shank_top)`, it partitions that span across the boundaries of the stated shank (or drawn neck) and the holder body, taking the wider radius on every sub-span.
- Tightened `HolderStack::shank_bands`'s `beside` boundary check in `crates/tools/src/neck.rs` by `1e-9` mm so floating-point dust at a split foot does not smear the holder radius below the foot.
- Passed `shank_with_body(&stored, body.as_ref(), neck)` from `crates/app/src/operation/tool_gate.rs` (`job_tool`) and `crates/app/src/fixture_struck.rs` (`op_hits`). `pocket_reach`, `verify`, fixture checks, and the post gate now judge the stated shank below a beside-shank holder foot and still block on real holder collisions from the foot upward.
- Added decision note `docs/decisions/2199-holder-beside-shank.md`.

## Cause

Two bugs compounded when a holder started at or below `shank_top`:
1. `HolderProfile::enclose` called inclusive `reach_over(fl, shank_top)`, so a holder starting at `shank_top` widened `judged.shank_d` (#2180).
2. `job_tool` and `op_hits` discarded `stored.shank_d` once `tool_body::judged` replaced `tool` with the enclosed cylinder, leaving `neck` empty and causing `pocket_reach`, `verify`, fixture checks, and `post` to judge the holder diameter all the way down to `flute_len` (#2199).

## Tests

- Pins (red before fix, green after fix):
  - `holder_profile::tests::a_band_touching_only_the_shank_top_does_not_widen_the_judged_shank` (`camcraft-tools`)
  - `neck::tests::shank_with_body_splits_only_above_a_holder_foot_beside_the_shank`, `shank_with_body_keeps_neck_untouched_when_holder_starts_at_shank_top`, `shank_with_body_never_shrinks_stated_shank_or_neck` (`camcraft-tools`)
  - `crates/app/tests/tool_body_beside_shank.rs` (`t31_holder_beside_shank_allows_3d_pocket_below_holder_foot_and_refuses_at_foot`, `t31_verify_judges_shank_at_6_35_below_38_1_and_catches_real_holder_hit`, `t31_fixture_law_judges_shank_below_holder_foot_and_catches_holder_beside_shank`, `issue_2180_cone_touching_only_shank_top_never_widens_shank`, `holder_narrower_than_stated_shank_never_shrinks_shank_judgement`)
- Mutation checks:
  - Reverted `crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs` to `upstream/main`: `a_band_touching_only_the_shank_top_does_not_widen_the_judged_shank` failed (`left: 60.0`, `right: 6.0`); passed after restore.
  - Reverted `crates/app/src/operation/tool_gate.rs` to `upstream/main`: `t31_holder_beside_shank_allows_3d_pocket_below_holder_foot_and_refuses_at_foot` and `t31_verify_judges_shank_at_6_35_below_38_1_and_catches_real_holder_hit` failed; both passed after restore.
  - Reverted `crates/app/src/fixture_struck.rs` to `upstream/main`: `t31_fixture_law_judges_shank_below_holder_foot_and_catches_holder_beside_shank` failed; passed after restore.
  - Removed `- 1e-9` boundary tolerance in `HolderStack::shank_bands`'s `beside` check: `shank_with_body_splits_only_above_a_holder_foot_beside_the_shank` failed (`r: 17.5` smeared down to `14.478`); passed after restore.
- Suites and checks run after final Rust edit:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed (`wall 0.7 min, 2 step(s), 0 failed`).

title: fix(post): apply stored script options for named posts and warn on mismatch
body:
## What changed

- Added `posting::resolve_cps` to return both the resolved `PostRef` and script text for a post name or `.cps` path. Kept `resolve_cps_text` as a thin wrapper.
- Added `posting::post_script_for_post_with_options` and `posting_mounts::post_mounts_for_post_with_options`. Threaded the optional `PostRef` through single-mount (`post_script_as`) and multi-mount (`post_each`) posting into `program_options_for_script`.
- Added `setup_post_options::same_post` and updated `setup_post_options::script_for_post`. `PostRef::Builtin` and `PostRef::Named` match via `post_key`, and `PostRef::File` entries fall back to canonical path matching via `std::fs::canonicalize`.
- Added `setup_post_options::unapplied_script_warning` and wired it into `script::api::v_post` (shared by MCP `post`, JS `cam.post`, and CLI `process --cps`).
- Added optional `"warning"` output to `script::report::posted_view`, `PostResult` docs in `script/mod.rs`, `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts`, and `env.logs` for CLI runs when stored `script_options` of the document or a setup's configured post did not apply.
- Recorded the design choice in `docs/decisions/2190-named-post-script-options.md`.

## Cause

`script::api::v_post` called `posting::resolve_cps_text`, which discarded the resolved `PostRef`. It then called `post_mounts_script_with_options`, which passed `post: None` into `post_script_as` and omitted `explicit_post` in `post_each`. Because `program_options_for_script` saw `post: None`, it skipped `setup_post_options::script_for_post` and silently dropped all stored `PostScriptOptions`. `script_for_post` also lacked canonical path fallback for `PostRef::File` keys, and nothing warned when an explicit post left configured `script_options` unapplied.

## Tests

Pinning tests added in `crates/app/tests/post_script_options.rs` (all 4 failed on unchanged `upstream/main` `e3ca44fa7`, and all 7 tests in `post_script_options` pass after the fix):

title: fix(2d): re-trace fitted contour arcs along exit-point overlap
body:
## What changed

- `contour_start::exit_at` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs`) now projects the exit pick onto the fitted walk `walk` instead of the raw polyline `poly`.
- `nearest_on_walk` and `arc_foot` find the closest point across both `Seg::Line` and `Seg::Arc` moves, snapping within `1e-5` mm (`SNAP_EPS`) of endpoints to prevent sub-lattice slivers.
- `extend_walk` appends the walk's own lines and arcs along the overlap so rounded corners and fillets re-cut the same moves as the first lap.
- When an exit pick lands strictly inside a segment, `extend_walk` splits that segment on the first lap as well so both laps emit identical CL moves and the lead-out shares an exact vertex.
- Added the decision record in `docs/decisions/2195-contour-exit-arcs.md`.

## Cause

The first lap of a closed 2D contour runs through `fit_arcs_sided` (and `fillet_corners` when enabled), which turns rounded corners into `Seg::Arc` moves. `exit_at` previously projected onto and extended from the raw polyline `poly` (`Seg::Line`), emitting straight chords that lie inside and out of phase with the verifier's `arc_chords` tessellation. `verify::crossing` convicted those chords against the first lap's arc and blocked posting.

## Tests

Pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_start.rs`:
- `an_exit_past_a_rounded_corner_retraces_the_corner_arc_with_no_crossing`
- `an_exit_inside_a_rounded_corner_arc_splits_both_laps_with_no_crossing`
- `an_exit_on_an_oblique_wall_and_across_a_blended_corner_has_no_crossing`

Mutation checks:
- Restored `upstream/main` `contour_start.rs`: all three new pinning tests failed with XY feed crossings (including `[5, 15]` and `[5, 17]` on the #2195 fixture).
- Disabled only the first-lap interior split in `extend_walk`: `an_exit_inside_a_rounded_corner_arc_splits_both_laps_with_no_crossing` failed with XY crossings.
- Restored the fix: all 14 tests in `contour_start` passed.

Gate and lint on the final code:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`camcraft-motion --lib` and `--test contour_start`, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green with zero warnings.

## Goldens moved

None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Did not run `camcraft-app` / MCP / `post` end-to-end tests or the GUI (only `camcraft-motion` changed).
- Did not run `batch` or `release` gate tiers.

## Overlaps

- PR #1822: touches `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs` (`pick_ring`) and `crates/motion/tests/contour_start.rs` (tab tests) — touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.

title: fix(post): split near-180 R arcs and verify chord <= 2|R| after rounding
body:
## What changed
- Updated `emitArcWithRadius` in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/haas.cps`, `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, `assets/posts/tormach.cps`, and `assets/posts/grblhal.cps`.
- The helper computes both endpoint radii `r0` and `r1`, uses the mean `r = (r0 + r1) * 0.5`, and falls back to I/J/K when `Math.abs(r0 - r1) > Math.min(0.02, Math.max(0.002, r * 0.005))`.
- The helper splits full and near-360 degree arcs (`full || sweep >= 2 * Math.PI - Math.PI / 9`) into 4 quadrant segments, splits near-180 degree arcs (`Math.abs(sweep - Math.PI) <= Math.PI / 9`) into 2 ~90 degree segments, and interpolates axis `h` linearly per segment.
- `buildSegs` checks every segment after output rounding (`fu(...)` relative to `[orgX, orgY, orgZ]`): `rp > 0`, `chord > 0`, `chord <= 2 * rp - 1e-7`, and `chord <= 2 * rp * 0.99` when unsplit (`count === 1`, re-splitting into quadrants if triggered).
- When any guard fails, `emitArcWithRadius` returns `false` before calling `block(...)`, so `onCircular` falls back cleanly to I/J/K without partial output or stale plane state.
- Added `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs` to pin all six posts and recorded the trade-offs in `docs/decisions/2191-radius-arcs-180.md`.

## Cause
- `emitArcWithRadius` computed `R` only from `from -> center` and split only exact full circles (`< 1e-5`).
- Helix half-turns from the 1 micron lattice carry slight endpoint radius differences and 180 degree sweeps, so separate rounding of `X`/`Y`/`Z` (`wo(...)`) and `R` (`w("R", ...)`) wrote `R1.235`/`R1.234` and chords longer than `2|R|` (`2.469 > 2.468`), while magnifying center drift near 180 degrees.

## Tests
- Pins in `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs` (across `fanuc`, `haas`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm`, `tormach`, `grblhal`):
  - `helix_half_turns_use_reachable_r_and_stay_on_circle` (red before fix, green after)
  - `near_180_and_full_circle_arcs_in_all_planes_hold_chord_and_center` (red before fix, green after)
  - `inch_and_nonzero_origin_arcs_hold_after_rounding` (red before fix, green after)
  - `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk` (red before fix, green after)
  - `recorded_arc_streams_post_valid_r_arcs`
- Mutation checks on `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (each guard reverted -> red, restored -> green):
  - Removing the radius-mismatch guard failed `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk` (`fanuc/mismatch`); restoring passed all 5 tests.
  - Disabling the near-180 / near-360 split and `0.99` chord guard (keeping the old 2-way full-circle split) failed 4 tests; restoring passed all 5 tests.
  - Removing the post-rounding `rp > 0` and `chord <= 2 * rp` checks failed `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk` (`fanuc/tiny_inch`); restoring passed all 5 tests.
- Checks after final edit:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test radius_arcs`: 5 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green (0 warnings).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green (0 warnings).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`:
  - `[01] post suites` (42 suites): passed in 23s.
  - `[02] app suites` (68 suites): 67 suites passed. `first_4axis_part::the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program` failed at `machine::check_document` (`"Flat A-90: inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting"`). The other 3 tests in `first_4axis_part` passed. That single failure is pre-existing on `upstream/main` (`e3ca44fa7`) because `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` still carries v2 stamps under `camcraft-op-stamp-v3` (#2198, open PR #2200).

## Goldens moved
None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised
- Full `batch` and `release` gate tiers, UI suites (no UI files changed), and re-running `app suites` on top of PR #2200 (`examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` stamp v3 regeneration).

## Overlaps
Touches the same `.cps` files in different functions (whichever merges second refreshes):
- `#2162` (`assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `reversedLoneXRotary`)
- `#2136` (`assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/haas.cps`, `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `onParameter`, `startPreamble`, `endPreamble`)
- `#2048` and `#1821` (`assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/haas.cps`, `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `onCycle`)
- `#1738` lists the post files in GitHub's diff from its older base PR `#1717` and changes no posted G-code.
No open PR changes `emitArcWithRadius` or `onCircular`.

title: feat(sim): calculate the playback stock removal before playback
body:
## What changed

The traced playback worker now cuts the whole program one time when the transport starts. It keeps keyframes of the cut stock at a fixed stride. After that, a jump forward or back restores the keyframe at or before the playhead and cuts at most one stride. The program is not cut again during playback.

- `crates/app/src/stock_play_precalc.rs` (new): `Precalc` state, `FieldPlay::begin_precalc` / `precalc_step`, keyframe thinning to a byte budget (512 MiB, at most 1024 keyframes, at least 64 moves apart).
- `crates/app/src/stock_play_worker_precalc.rs` (new): `PlayWorker::spawn_precalc`, `precalc()`, `cancel_precalc()`, and the calculation loop on the worker thread.
- `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`, `stock_play_worker.rs`: a seek restores a keyframe that is more than one stride ahead, not only one behind. A `moves_cut` counter measures the replay law.
- `crates/ui/src/actions.rs`: the transport starts the worker with the calculation.
- `crates/ui/src/play_precalc.rs` (new), `egui_app/shell.rs`: a line under the transport shows the progress and a Cancel button. A stopped calculation shows "incomplete" with the reason.
- `docs/decisions/2181-sim-precalc.md`: the design and the dropped options.

The stamp is `doc_version`. Each command retires the worker and frees its keyframes (an operation delete included). The keyframes are display only. The Deviate verdict and the post gate do not read them.

## Readings

Release, dense face (100 mm block, stepover 0.5, stepdown 0.5, `DEFAULT_TEXELS`), `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`:

- 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64
- keyframe memory 444940288 bytes (424 MiB, under the 512 MiB budget)
- calculation time 23.9 s

During the calculation the sheet stands and the line shows the progress. Follow-up #2193 serves frames during the calculation. Follow-up #2194 lowers the keyframe memory.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`:
- `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position` (bit-identical cut layer at each move, forward and back jumps mixed)
- `a_jump_after_the_calculation_cuts_at_most_one_stride` (no new full calculation)
- `the_keyframes_stay_within_the_memory_budget`
- `a_stopped_calculation_leaves_exact_keyframes_and_cuts_the_rest_live`
- `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (`posting::verification_gate` is equal before and after)
- `a_cancelled_calculation_is_incomplete_by_name_and_playback_goes_on`
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (ignored, heavy lane, the reading above)

`crates/ui/src/play_precalc_tests.rs`:
- `the_readout_says_progress_and_incomplete_and_nothing_when_done`
- `an_edit_of_the_operation_retires_the_stored_calculation`

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: app suites ok (`--lib`, `stock_play`, `stock_play_partial`, `stock_play_precalc`). ui suites: one failure, `stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape`. This test also fails on main (#2170).
- Also run: `fidelity_copies`, ui lib `play_bench`, `field_view`, `view_pass`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI was not started. The transport line and the Cancel button are not seen on screen; no screenshot.
- The reading uses one large fixture only.

## Overlap

#2182 changes other hunks of `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` (status strings). The two PRs do not stack.

Changelog: Simulation playback calculates the stock removal one time before it plays, then replays it, so a jump on the timeline does not lag. A line under the transport shows the progress and can cancel the calculation.

Effort: high (issue label effort:max; an Opus worker of the high tier works it by the maintainer's order; no escalation)

Fixes #2181

title: feat(fixtures): turn a fixture by quarter turns or a typed angle
body:
## What changed

- New undoable command `TurnFixture` (`crates/app/src/commands/fixture_turn.rs`). It turns one fixture about world X, Y or Z through the fixture origin. The write is a `MoveFixture`, so plate riders turn with the fixture.
- Quarter turns write exact quaternion components (`settle_rot`). A turn that changes nothing (0 or 360 degrees) is refused. This obeys #2177.
- A part or the stock that touched the fixture before the turn stays in position. The warning names each one (`fixture_clash::held_by`).
- The turn does not make toolpaths stale. The post gate reads the turned fixture live. A turn into the tool path blocks the post with "strikes a fixture".
- Fixtures page place draft: "Place yaw" is replaced by "Tilt about X (roll)", "Tilt about Y (pitch)" and "Turn about Z (yaw)". Six buttons "Turn X+" .. "Turn Z-" apply a quarter turn immediately. The row text shows roll and pitch when the fixture is not upright.
- New MCP tool `turn_fixture` (`crates/app/src/mcp/fixture_turn_tools.rs`), with a row in the `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2174-fixture-turns.md`.

title: feat(ui): drag rings in Rotate mode turn the selected part
body:
Stacked on #1330. This branch starts from the head of #1330 (`58df4b729`, fork branch `mkinney:issue/1198-drag-to-move`) with `origin/main` merged in. Until #1330 merges, the diff shows the commits of #1330 too. The new work is commit `043b7e0a9`.

## What changed
- The viewport bar has a new Rotate button after Move. Move and Rotate are mutually exclusive. A toggle cancels the live drag of the other mode.
- With Rotate on, the one selected part shows three rings round its bounding-box centre. Each ring is square to one shown axis. The ring radius is a constant 60 px on the screen. A press within 6 px of a ring grabs the nearest ring.
- The drag angle is the point where the cursor ray meets the ring plane, measured about the centre. The angle is unwrapped, so a drag can go past 180 degrees. During the drag the part preview turns and the bar shows `Turn about Z: +35.0°`. The world does not change during the drag.
- The release queues one `CommandKind::TurnModelBy { name, axis, angle_rad }`. The drain runs the existing `MoveModel`, so the turn is one undo step. The generated operations go stale and the stock follows the part, as for a typed turn.
- An aligned setup turns the part about the axis that the user sees (the turn goes back through the setup alignment).
- Escape cancels the turn with no history step. A turn that ends at its start angle queues nothing and writes no rotation noise (#2177).
- A bad axis, a non-finite angle or a missing part is refused by name on the status line.
- New files: `crates/ui/src/turn_drag.rs` (the drag law), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turn_handles.rs` (the paint), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_tests.rs` (the bar tests moved out to keep `viewport_bar.rs` near 400 lines).
- No new app command, so no new MCP tool. MCP `move_model` already sets the rotation.

## How the stale path is pinned
`body_turn::a_ring_drag_is_one_undoable_turn_that_stales_the_path_and_carries_the_stock` drags the Z ring on the seeded document. Before the drag, `camcraft_app::posting::program_ops` returns `Ok`. After the release, it returns an `Err` that contains "regenerate", so the post refuses. One undo makes the history clean again and `program_ops` returns `Ok` again. The same test checks that the stock box still holds the turned part. The app-level pin `crates/app/tests/commands_undo.rs::a_moved_part_marks_generated_ops_stale_and_undo_clears_it` already covers a pure rotation in the stale stamp.

## Pinning tests
- `egui_app::tests::body_turn::*` (5 tests): rings only in Rotate mode at a constant size; one undoable turn that makes the path stale and carries the stock; Escape cancels; a zero turn adds nothing; empty space still orbits.
- `turn_drag_tests::*` (6 tests): the angle under the cursor, a drag past half a turn, no command for a press off the rings or a turn in place, the centre stays in place, a turned setup, refusals by name.
- `egui_app::viewport_bar::tests::move_and_rotate_modes_never_share_the_part`.

## Readings
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on head `043b7e0a9`: ui lib 954 passed, 1 failed; boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_files, waterjet_tool all green. The one failure is `stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape`, which also fails on main (#2170, fix PR #2171).
- Clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised
- No hand test in the live window. The screenshots come from the kittest harness render of the shipping shell with the GPU viewport, at 1280x720.
- No angle snapping (not asked for; see `docs/decisions/2047-drag-to-rotate.md`).
- `shell.rs` was already longer than 400 lines before this change; this PR adds 11 lines to it.

## Screenshots
Before (Move mode of #1330 on this branch: the move balls, no rings):
![before move](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/before-move.png?raw=true)
After (Rotate mode, a Z-ring drag of +35 degrees in progress):
![after rotate](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/after-rotate.png?raw=true)

title: fix(fixtures): locate the stock on an existing vise
body:
## What changed

The locate took mates on the part only. Thus a user could not seat the stock on a vise that was already placed. The fixture collision checks and the carried-workholding check then read a stock place that nobody set.

- `fixture_locate`: `LocateSpec` has a new field `body` (`LocateBody::Part` is the default, `LocateBody::Stock` is new). `stock_of` finds the stock of the fixture's setup. With the stock held, the mates are on the stock, in the stock's own pose.
- `LocatePart`: with the stock held, the part moves and the stock follows it (stock-follow law). The part keeps its place in the blank. The locate is one undo step.
- Refusals by name: a stock locate with no part, a setup with no stock, a mate on the wrong body. A square stock re-fits round a turned part with the allowance of each setup side. If that re-fit leaves the stock faces off the mates, `stock_lands` refuses the locate ("would not land on the mates").
- Review fix (head `32102879d`): `stock_lands` (now in `crates/app/src/fixture_locate_land.rs`) judges each picked stock face, not only the box of the stock. The face is placed where the mates put it. The followed stock must have facets that face the same way (`NORMAL_TOL` = 1e-4 on 1 - cos of the angle, about 0.8 degree) and lie on that plane (`LEN_TOL_MM` = 1e-4 mm). These facets must cover the face area (`FACE_AREA_REL_TOL` = 0.1 %) and each facet centre of the face. A picked stock vertex must be a corner of the followed stock. A failure is refused in `LocatePart::new`. The message names the stock face and the fixture face: "mate N: <stock face> of the stock '<stock>' would stand across the plane of, not flat on, <fixture face> of '<fixture>' - ... locate it without a turn, or locate the part".
- MCP: `locate_part` takes `"body": "stock"` (the default is `"part"`). `list_features` lists the faces of a stock.
- UI: the locate form shows "Place by: Stock faces / Part faces". It holds the stock by default when the fixture's setup has a stock. While the stock is held, the picks pass over the parts inside the stock, so a stock face round a part can be picked.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2173-locate-stock-on-vise.md`.

## Effect on checks and posted output

No change for existing projects and scripts: the API and MCP default stay `Part`. The new path moves the part and its stock as a part locate does. The existing locate tests pass unchanged.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/fixture_locate_stock_body.rs`:
  - `the_stock_locates_on_an_existing_vise_and_undo_puts_it_back`
  - `the_fixture_collision_check_reads_the_located_stock` (`fixture_clash::after_fixture_move` reads the located stock)
  - `a_stock_that_would_miss_its_mates_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_part_stays_the_default_body`
  - `mcp_locate_part_seats_the_stock_by_its_feature_ids`
- `crates/app/tests/fixture_locate_stock_cylinder.rs` (review fix):
  - `a_cylinder_cap_mated_across_its_plane_is_refused` (the review repro: D20 x H20 cylinder, cap on a +X stop face)
  - `a_cylinder_cap_mated_on_the_floor_lands_at_the_right_height` (the legal twin; the collision check reads the landed stock)
  - `a_turned_cylinder_cap_on_the_floor_is_judged_by_its_face_and_lands` (a re-fit with new facets goes through the face check)
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::locate_tests::the_fixtures_page_locates_the_stock_on_the_vise`

## Readings

Review fix, head `32102879d` (on the PR base, no merge of main):
- `camcraft-app`: `fixture_locate` 11/11, `fixture_locate_stock` 3/3, `fixture_locate_stock_body` 5/5, `fixture_locate_stock_cylinder` 3/3, `fixture_plate_followups` 4/4, `mcp_setup` 9/9, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_lay_face` 1/1.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean. The fix changes no UI code.
- Mutation checks: `face_lands` always true makes `a_cylinder_cap_mated_across_its_plane_is_refused` fail. `face_lands` always false makes `a_turned_cylinder_cap_on_the_floor_is_judged_by_its_face_and_lands` fail. With the rigid-carry shortcut off, all the stock suites above still pass.

First head `c492f7006`:

- `camcraft-app`: `fixture_locate` 11/11, `fixture_locate_stock` 3/3, `fixture_locate_stock_body` 5/5, `fixture_plate_followups` 4/4, `mcp_setup` 9/9, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_lay_face` 1/1.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: 933 pass, 1 fail. The fail is `stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape`; it also fails on main (#2170, fix in PR #2171).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick` did not complete in 50 min on a busy machine (my `timeout` stopped it; no test failed). I ran its parts above one by one.
- `one_pick_rule::locate_and_points_drafts_take_box_corners_as_points` now sets the body to Part. Its document has a stock, and the test pins the part corner.

## Not exercised

- A stock locate in a setup with a turned frame (the tests use the default setup frame).
- A cylinder stock with a turn that is not a multiple of the facet angle. The box check refuses it (the turned facets change the box). This refusal is safe, but a user can find it too strict.
- A stock vertex mate after a re-fit (the vertex branch of the check has no test of its own).
- The camcraft-ui suites after the review fix (the fix changes no UI code).
- The GUI by hand (no screenshots).

## Screenshots

Same document in each image: a 100 x 60 x 10 mm vise, a 20 x 10 x 8 mm part away from it, and a box stock round the part. The Fixtures page is open and "Locate part..." is armed. The images come from the test harness render of the full window at 1440x960.

Before (main): the locate form has no "Place by" choice. It locates the part only.

title: fix(sim): simulate a stock held in a vise; model quarter-turned stock
body:
## What changed

- `MoveModel` (and so `LocatePart`) keeps the stock's own rotation when the move does not turn the part. Before, the float noise of the locate solve (about 5e-14) became a stored stock rotation, and the stock sim refused the stock in a vise.
- `stock_follow::sim_frame` is the one law for the stock frame of the simulation. `stock_sim::stock_grid`, `stock_sim_held::first_body` / `first_field` and `stock_view::stock_facets` read it.
  - An unturned stock is unchanged.
  - A box turned by a quarter-turn multiple (within 1e-9) is its unturned twin with the sides swapped.
  - An upright cylinder is an unturned cylinder.
  - A from-model stock is read from its placed mesh at any turn.
  - An oblique box and a laid cylinder are refused by name (`OBLIQUE_STOCK`, `LAID_CYLINDER`).
- The UI says a simulation refusal one time, in plain words. The uncut stock stays drawn.
- Review fix (commit 465638b09): four suites used a stock turned a quarter about Z to make the program sim refuse. The device is now a turn of 1e-6 rad about Z (`OBLIQUE`), which the sim refuses by name. See "Readings".
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2177-square-stock-sim.md`.

## Readings

Effect: a project whose stock had locate noise or a quarter turn was "not judged" by the stock sim. Now the sim judges it, and a gouge that the sim finds can block the post. No posted G-code changes. No golden `.nc` / `.cl` file and no snapshot PNG changes.

The review found 9 red tests. In each case the PR is correct and the test device was wrong:

| Test (suite) | Reading |
|---|---|
| `deep-Engrave-true`, `low-top-Engrave-true`, `wall-Engrave-true` (`engrave_law`) | The cut is a real gouge (the operation convicts it too). The post was refused. The sim now judges the quarter-turned stock, so its gouge clause leads the message. |
| `through` and `stock-through` / `stock-web` Engrave (`mark_floor` lines 160, 253) | Same: a cut through the 2 mm plate. The sim convicts it correctly. |
| `into-a-trace-true` (`neighbour_law`) | Same: the flank enters part A by 0.3 mm. The sim finds 0.3 mm on A, as on the aligned stock. |
| `low-stock-face-true`, `slot-false-true`, `engrave-false-true` (`stock_source_law`) | Same: cuts off the stock into the part. |

The `by_op` checks are kept and are not loosened. They pin that the operation's own gouge blocks the post when the sim does not judge. Each `by_op` check now also asserts that the sim refuses the stock with `OBLIQUE_STOCK`, so the device cannot become silent. The fixture box check takes 1e-4 mm in X and Y for the 1e-6 rad turn (the corners move by less than 6e-5 mm). Z stays at 1e-9.

## Pinning tests

- `stock_in_vise_sim` (2 tests): a located stock in a vise is simulated; an oblique stock is refused by name.
- New, one in each suite: `a_quarter_turned_stock_is_judged_by_the_program_sim` in `engrave_law`, `mark_floor`, `neighbour_law`, `stock_source_law`. The quarter-turned stock is judged, its gouge blocks the post, and a legal mark posts.
- The MCP parity test of `stock_source_law` moved to the new suite `stock_source_law_mcp` (the 400-line law). The `#[test]` count grows by 4: 28 to 32 in the five suites.

## Gate (on the PR head, not merged with main)

- `engrave_law` 10/10, `mark_floor` 7/7, `neighbour_law` 7/7, `stock_source_law` 7/7, `stock_source_law_mcp` 1/1.
- `stock_in_vise_sim` 2/2, `post_not_judged` 4/4, `area_controls` 13/13, `pocket_recognition` 11/11 (they share the changed test modules).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The review run (trial merge with main `1f15f98e7`) covers the rest: app lib 353, ui lib 949 and 13 ui suites, `stock_sim_document`, `stock_view`, `rotary_field_parity`, `posting`, `verify`, `stock_source_verdict`.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real control or machine.
- No GUI run for this fix.
- Not built merged with the current `main`: the PR merges cleanly, and the current `main` has a debug build error in work by a different agent.
- The combination with PR #2184 (`fixture_locate_stock`, `fixture_locate_stock_body`, `stock_in_vise_sim`) is not run. Run them after the second of the two merges.

Changelog: The simulation now shows and judges a stock held in a vise after a locate, and a stock turned by a quarter turn; a stock turned off the machine axes is refused in plain words.

Effort: high

Fixes #2177

title: fix(sim): draw a drawn holder profile as drawn
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/sim_tool_body.rs`: the viewport simulation draws a drawn (spun) holder with its own outline (`SpunProfile::outline`). Tapers and arcs show as drawn. Before, it showed the stepped bands that the collision laws read.
- With a drawn holder, the simulation also draws the shank as stored. The judged record widens the shank to each band that touches the shank top (`HolderProfile::enclose`). Before, a Ø44 holder foot made the shank look Ø44 down to the flutes.
- New `JudgedOutline::with_drawn(drawn, stored)`. It refuses (`OutlineError::PastJudged`) a drawn point outside every band at its height, and a stored cutter that is wider or longer than the judged one. The picture is never wider than the check.
- A machine-default holder (#828) and an imported STL/STEP body keep the band drawing.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2176-sim-draws-drawn-holder.md`.

## Readings

- The trace is on the issue. All consumers already read one landed body: the collision checks, the verify/post gate (`kept_rejudge` -> `collect_job` -> `job_tool`) and the simulation. Only the picture was wrong. The issue stays P3.
- Posted G-code and the check results do not change for existing projects. Only the display changes. The checks still read the bands and the widened shank. These are never smaller than the drawn shape.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/sim_tool_drawn_holder.rs`:
- `a_drawn_holder_is_drawn_with_its_own_radii_and_lengths` (the profile of the issue picture)
- `a_drawn_cone_is_drawn_as_a_cone_and_judged_as_its_enclosing_band` (moved from `sim_tool_body.rs`, where it pinned the old band drawing; the test count stays the same)
- `a_profile_edit_redraws_the_holder_and_undo_restores_it`
- `checks_verify_and_simulation_read_one_holder_shape`

Quick gate (debug, `-j 6`): `sim_tool_drawn_holder` 4/4, `sim_tool_body` 6/6, `tool_body_judged` 8/8, `tool_neck_laws` 4/4, `tool_spun_profile` 7/7, `holder_library` 12/12. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The `camcraft-ui` crate was not built or tested. Its sim test (`egui_app/tests/tool_body.rs`) uses an imported STL body, which keeps the band drawing. No public item that it uses changed.
- No GUI screenshot. The change is in the tool-frame mesh only.
- A spun body with `machine_default` set is not pinned. It keeps the old path.

## Follow-up

The judged shank is widened by a band that only touches the shank top (`reach_over` uses inclusive bounds). That can be over-conservative for the shank laws. This PR does not change any law.

Changelog: The simulation now draws a drawn tool holder with its own profile (tapers and arcs), and the shank with its stored diameter, in place of stepped cylinders.

Effort: high

Fixes #2176
