title: fix(2d): enter over the stock standing above a 2D op's Top instead of rapiding into it
body:
## What changed

A 2D ladder whose Top is below the material standing over it - typically Top set to the first real cut under a faced top, to skip the air pass at the faced top (#514 stays as decided) - now **enters safely**: it rapids no lower than the plunge height over the remaining material and feeds the rest of the way down to its first level. Before, the entry rapided to Top + the plunge height, inside the uncut stock, and verify refused the op (`rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock`), so the air pass could not be avoided.

- `camcraft_motion::approach::Approach` gains `material_top: Option<f64>` - a runtime-only field like `center_cutting`, never saved - with `entry_top()` / `carries_stock()`.
- The ladders read it for their first descent and their plunge-law guards: `levels` (Pocket, 2D Adaptive spiral, Offset, Circular via `Motion::with_top`; the Slot reads it too but is not carried yet), `adaptive_troch` (2D Adaptive trochoidal), and the Contour's bore side, wall-side arc entry, graze, tab and ring dives.
- `camcraft_app::operation::top_stock::carried` reads the material top over the op's region - the declared stock's highest surface there, lowered by what the program ahead cut (the reading #104's "Top below stock" note already made); a Contour beside a wall (Outside/Auto) reads the band one tool diameter around its region (`contour_reach`), never the part's own footprint.
- **Only where needed:** `generate` first makes the op as before; only if that path's entry rapids down under the material standing under the tool's disc (`top_stock::dives_into`: the declared stock's own top there, lowered by the program ahead - the rapid law's #1091 and #96 re-reads) is it generated again with the top carried. Pocket, 2D Adaptive, Offset, Circular and Contour (selection and model sources; upright frames only). A finish entering through what a rough cleared keeps its path byte for byte.
- The op says so: `Carried stock: the operation's top Z.. is below the material over its region (Z..) - the first descent starts over that material and feeds down; the first level engages .. mm`, in place of the #104 warning for those kinds. Slot, trochoidal slot, chamfer, trace and 3D kinds keep the #104 note and the rapid law's refusal.
- Top on the material: nothing carried, the path is byte-identical (pinned).

## Severity (re-judged from the code)

Not P1: the rapid law convicts this entry (`RapidInStock` holds the post) and the #96/#1091 re-reads only acquit what the program ahead really cleared - a legal program refused with a workaround, P3 by the table (labels left to the maintainer). A silent case next to it - a clearance plane set inside the stock is never judged by the rapid law and posts - is filed as **#2121 (P1)**.

## How tested

title: docs(turning): record why the laid flank pass ends stay short of D
body:
## What changed
- New decision file `docs/decisions/1896-thread-pass-ends.md`. It records why the laid flank passes keep their present ends. This is the second "Done means" choice of #1896.
- The pin `every_pass_runs_to_the_posted_end_z_inside_the_root_pass` keeps its assertion. Its comment now names the decision.
- No production code changed.

## Cause
A control that runs G76 ends every flank pass at D. The kernel lays each flank pass as whole half-turns, shifted by its flank offset. Thus a shallower pass ends short of D by `(k - depth) * tan(a/2)`.

## Why the present ends stay
- The kernel refuses a flank angle wider than the insert's half-angle. Thus the control's extra run-out stays inside the root pass's V at D. It is never deeper than the root pass and never passes D toward the chuck.
- G32 and G33 passes cut exactly the laid passes. The lathe stock simulation refuses helical passes by name, so no simulated stock differs.
- A partial helical arc to D ends off the meridian plane. The holder law, the rapid law, both lathe posts (`threadHalfTurn`) and the two thread verdicts read every thread arc as a meridian or antipodal half-turn. To change all of them is a large change to the safety surface for a P7 gain. The decision file lists each part.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_g76_sources`: 3 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test turning_thread_infeed -- plans_that_cannot_cut_refuse_by_name flank_infeed_shifts_each_pass_along_its_flank`: 2 passed. These pin the half-angle refusal that the containment proof uses.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (1 step).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No new pin and no mutation check: this PR changes no behaviour.

None.

- The partial-arc design was read in the code, not built. The earlier worker's held pin (`mkinney:issue/1896-thread-pass-ends`, commit 145dcc86) fails on main by design. This decision supersedes it.

None. The open draft #468 changes the thread pass loop, but this PR does not touch it.

title: fix(drilling): state the through-hole break-through and say where it goes
body:
## What changed

Through holes ran a hidden, fixed 1.0 mm past the part bottom (`THROUGH_CLEAR`; one pitch on a thread), not a parameter and not checked against what is under the part. Now:

- **A stated parameter.** Drill, Bore and Thread carry `break_through: Option<f64>` (mm). `None` is the kind's old figure - 1.0 mm for Drill and Bore, one pitch for an internal Thread - so every existing op generates and posts byte-identical and keeps its digest (written only when stated). It is a **Break-through** row (Default / a length in the document unit) in the hole kinds' Heights > Levels group, `break_through` in the project file and in the MCP params JSON (`add_operation` / `edit_operation` read the same DTO).
- **Kernels:** `drilling::CycleParams::through_clear`, `machining2d::ThreadParams::through_run`; the Bore already took `through_allowance`, now the op's value (and Detect holes' borability reads it too).
- **Said:** every op with a through hole notes `through holes run 1.000 mm past the part bottom (Break-through), the deepest to Z...` in the document unit.
- **Checked against what lies below:** with workholding or a table modelled in the setup, the fixture laws judge the tip - a break-through into modelled steel is a `FixtureHit` on the flute and holds the post (pinned with a spoil board modelled under the stock); air between modelled parallels stays legal. With nothing modelled, a tip under the stock bottom is **named, not refused**: `Break-through below stock: the through hole at (x, y) runs to Z.., .. under the stock bottom Z.. - whatever the stock sits on is cut there; model the parallels, spoil board or fixture under it ..., or lower the Break-through`. Refusing there would stop every through hole in a plate sawn to size, a program that posts today; the reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1557-through-break-through.md`.
- Negative / non-finite values are refused at creation (`sane`) and by the kernels; a stated value on a lathe's axial or cross Drill is refused by name.
- **Project file v63** (`PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63): an old reader must refuse a file rather than drop a stated break-through. If another open PR also takes v63, whichever merges second takes the next number.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`: `the_default_is_today_s_millimetre_and_is_said` (Drill and Bore: deepest Z -1.000, note, below-stock note), `a_stated_break_through_moves_the_deepest_feed` (0.3 mm and 0 for Drill, 0.3 for Bore), `a_negative_break_through_is_refused_at_creation`, `a_break_through_into_modelled_steel_under_the_stock_is_refused` (flute hit, post refused; 0 posts), `the_parameter_round_trips_the_file_and_the_mcp_params`.
- `operation::break_through` unit tests (deepest tip, below-stock note with and without steel, inch document).
- `machining2d::thread_tests::a_through_hole_runs_one_pitch_unless_the_break_through_is_stated`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion 455 s, app 1145 s, ui 65 s); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The user's end-cap project (a copy, `camcraft-cli process ... -o`): 8 ops ok, gate ok, the posted program is **byte-identical** to the v0.21.0 program (its four holes are `through: false` with a typed floor, so no break-through applies).

## UI evidence

The shipping shell renders the Drill, Bore and Thread Heights pages below. Before captures omit the new Break-through row (the pre-change page). After captures show the default and an explicit length. PNGs live only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

| Page | Before | After, default | After, stated mm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drill | [Before](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/drill-before.png) | [After](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/drill-after.png) | [Stated](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/drill-stated-mm.png) |
| Bore | [Before](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/bore-before.png) | [After](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/bore-after.png) | [Stated](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/bore-stated-mm.png) |
| Thread | [Before](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/thread-before.png) | [After](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/thread-after.png) | [Stated](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ae6183eb/2126/thread-stated-mm.png) |

Structural pins: `hole_break_through_default_controls_and_document_units` checks the Default checkbox, default text, explicit numeric field and mm/in unit lens for all three kinds, restores Default, and checks Heights-only placement. `external_thread_has_no_hole_break_through_control` checks external threads. Removing the row calls makes the first pin RED; restoring them makes both GREEN.

## Not exercised

- A tool-relative default (drill point length): not added, see the decision file.
- Lathe axial and cross holes keep `THROUGH_CLEAR` (a stated value is refused there).

Changelog: Drill, Bore and Thread state their through-hole Break-through (default 1.0 mm, one pitch for a thread; unchanged programs post identically); the op notes how far past the part bottom it runs and names a run under an unmodelled stock bottom; project file v63

title: feat(post): Sodick wire tank and flushing words from the machine file
body:
## What changed

- **Two optional wire-machine keys** (`crates/post/src/machine/edm_dielectric.rs`, new):
  - `edm.tank`: `submerged` or `non-submerged`.
  - `edm.flushing`: `high` or `low`.

  Unstated means the operator sets it at the control. An unknown word refuses the `.mch` file, the project's machine and the MCP patch, naming the key and the allowed words. Both keys are wire keys: a sinker that states one is refused.
- **Set through the existing undoable machine mount**: the Machine window's wire section has two new combos, Tank and Flushing (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_edm.rs`), and the MCP `edit_machine` merge patch takes the same keys. No new command or MCP tool was needed.
- **`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`** writes the 1998 Mark 21 manual's T words: T84 / T85 for high / low flushing, and T94 / T89 for submersed / non-submersed machining. They go after each threading (T91, or the operator's M00) and before the C word, flushing first, in the order of the manual's Program Example 1 (T84, T94, C451). The header says what is programmed and what is still the operator's. The T94 line warns that no fill or drain word is written. An unknown word is also refused by name in the post, and nothing is cut.
- **Unstated: posts as today.** The #617 golden `nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch.nc` is byte-identical (pinned).
- **`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps`** writes a header note when the tank or flushing is stated, because it has no word for either. A program that states neither is unchanged.
- **Machine mirror** (`crates/post/src/post/machine.rs`): a wire's `edm` gains `tank` / `flushing` only when they are stated.
- Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `site/content/guide/operations/operations-edm.md`. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1499-sodick-flushing.md`.

## New golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch_flushed.nc`

This is the #617 punch on a machine stating `tank: submerged, flushing: high`, posted through the app's gate. Its diff against the #617 golden is pinned by `sodick_wire_dielectric::a_submerged_high_flush_punch_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate`:
- The header line `(TANK FILL AND FLUSHING ARE NOT PROGRAMMED - SET THEM AT THE CONTROL)` is replaced by `(T94 SUBMERGED MACHINING AFTER THREADING - NO FILL OR DRAIN WORD IS WRITTEN - CHECK THE TANK IS FULL)` and `(T84 HIGH-PRESSURE FLUSHING AFTER THREADING)`.
- `T91` (the wire is threaded at the start hole) is followed by `T84` (high pressure flushing on, manual T-code table), then `T94` (switch to submersed machining, manual T-code table), then `C110` (the condition, after both, in the Program Example 1 order).

Every other line is unchanged.

## How tested

- `crates/post/tests/sodick_dielectric.rs` (7 tests):
  - every value's word, and that it comes after threading and before C;
  - the manual's order;
  - unstated posts as before;
  - an M00 threading without AWT;
  - an unknown word refused by name, with nothing cut;
  - two sections each restating the words;
  - the wire-iso note.
- `crates/app/tests/sodick_wire_dielectric.rs` (3 tests): the golden, the unchanged #617 golden, and the round trip through the serde / `.mch` file with the garbled word refused.
- `mcp_edit_machine::a_wire_tank_and_flushing_edit_is_one_undo_step_and_an_unknown_word_is_refused`: one undo step, unknown words refused with nothing changed, and a sinker refused.
- `edm_dielectric` unit tests, and the UI test `machine_wire_edm::the_wire_machine_editor_states_tank_and_flushing`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- Not run on a Sodick control.
- The relative order of T91 and T84 / T94 is this PR's reading (the decision file says why). The issue text says "T94, T91, T84", but the manual pages read here show T84 then T94 with no T91.
- The fill / drain / pump / wire-drive T codes are not written.

Overlap: #2120 (#1497) also edits `sodick-wire.cps`, in a different hunk (`onRapid`), so this PR is branched from main, not stacked. It does not overlap #1921.

title: feat(sinker): read a welded wall face as its vertical strips
body:
## What changed

- A welded smooth face (`FeatureSel::Patch`) can now be a cavity wall in "electrode from faces".
- The app expands the patch into its planar strips (`feature::patches`). Each strip is read like a planar pick (`sinker_faces::faces_of`).
- The new motion rule `sinker_cavity::welded_wall` checks each strip. Every strip must be a vertical plane.
- `cavity_of` then stands each strip on the floor ring, like any wall. Its other refusals apply to each strip.
- A strip that leans, or that is level, refuses the whole welded face. The message names the welded face and the strip.
- A stale patch id is refused with "no longer in the model: re-pick it".

## Cause

`face_of` returned a blank face marked `curved` for each patch pick. `check_face` then refused it as "a curved wall". The tangent wall band of a rounded-corner pocket welds into one patch. So a click on a rounded corner gave a pick that could not make an electrode.

## Tests

- `sinker_electrode_body::a_rounded_pockets_corners_picked_as_welded_faces_yield_the_strips_electrode` (new). The floor and the one welded face (20 strips: four flat walls and sixteen corner strips) give the same electrode as the planar-strip pick. The finish burn is judged clean. The welded face picked beside its own strips gives the same electrode. A stale patch is refused by name.
  - Red before the fix: "welded face 0xe26b11036b29702e of 'part' is a curved wall - an electrode is generated from planar walls only".
- `sinker_electrode_tests::a_welded_wall_is_read_strip_by_strip_and_a_leaning_strip_is_refused_by_name` (new, motion unit test). Two vertical strips read as the planar wall. A strip drafted 4.764 degrees is refused by name. A level strip and an empty weld are refused by name.
- `sinker_electrode::a_rounded_pockets_corner_picked_as_its_welded_face_is_refused_by_name` is now `..._reads_as_its_strips`. This change intentionally reverses its old expectation. It now asserts the same electrode as the planar pick.

Mutation checks:
- Old `sinker_faces.rs` put back: the app pins fail (red). Fix restored: they pass (green).
- The vertical guard in `welded_wall` disabled: the motion pin fails (red). Guard restored: it passes (green).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (motion lib, app lib, `sinker_electrode`, `sinker_electrode_body`, `sinker_electrode_mcp`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted G-code changes.

## Not exercised

- A real model from a CAD import with a welded wall. The fixture is a synthetic mesh built in code.
- A drafted or blended curved wall. It stays refused by name; a lofted electrode is not modelled.
- Not exercised on a real EDM control. Synthetic conditions only.

## Overlaps

None in the changed functions. #1738 lists `crates/app/src/operation/sinker_faces.rs` only because its base branch is stale. Against upstream/main it does not change that file. #1753 does not change these files.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1808-welded-walls.md`.

Changelog: Sinker EDM: "electrode from faces" accepts a rounded-corner wall picked as its welded face; a welded wall that leans is refused by name (#1808)

Fixes #1808

title: fix(post): Sodick wire refuses a lean before the first rapid; 4-axis refusal kept
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`: a `WireU` / `WireV` stated before (or on) a section's first positioning move was cleared by `onRapid`, so the post wrote `G40 G00`, `T91`, the `C` word and `G01` as if the wire stood upright (the gap the last Codex run reported on #1497). That lean is now refused by name ("a leaning positioning move (upper guide offset)") and the whole section is neither threaded nor cut. The next section posts as before.
- The 4-axis refusal (no G74 / G75, no U V) **stays**, which the issue's "Done means" allows. `docs/decisions/1497-sodick-four-axis.md` records what the public Sodick manual confirms and what it leaves open. The manual (1998, Mark 21 / EX21) gives U V as offsets from X Y. For 4-axis, X Y lie on the part's bottom plane, and Table To Program / Table To Next are heights measured from the worktable. The "absolute mode" half of the U V sentence is not explained, and the manual gives no G74 example. Camcraft's stream carries the lower guide's X Y and the upper guide's offset. Neither the machine file nor the stream states the worktable height, so the guide-plane values cannot be converted to Sodick's planes from stated values. Writing them unconverted would post a wrong 4-axis cut.
- The `sodick_alc400g::a_tapered_punch_is_refused_at_post_while_the_file_states_no_guide_heights` failure that stopped the two Codex runs is **fixed on main** (PR #1857, commit 0e1f3709). It passes on `ce59ef446`, and the whole `sodick_alc400g` suite passes in this PR's quick gate.

New `crates/post/tests/sodick_four_axis.rs` (5 tests, synthetic CNC streams):

title: fix(motion): hold rest Adaptive air feed and retracts to a budget
body:
**Stacked on #2112** (rest Adaptive, `mkinney:issue/2031-rest-adaptive`, head 71a7fee47). This PR's own change is its last commit (ee0405765). Until #2112 merges, the diff against main also shows #2112's commits. Merge #2112 first. Not stacked on #2114 (#2113's pins); the two touch different hunks of `tests/rest_adaptive/sim.rs`.

## What changed

All in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/`:

1. **Retrace lead** (`rest/leads.rs`).
   - A rest pass can now be reached by going back along the pass just cut: the same chords reversed, which the exact-sign crossing law reads as a collinear retrace and never a crossing. It stops at the new run's start where the last pass went over it; otherwise it goes to that pass's wall landing and on along the wall.
   - Every lead is offered stay-down first, least air first; retract leads keep their old order.
   - The old wall stretch is still offered. Every lead is still asked the centre-area law, the crossing law and the load walk.
   - The retrace is a feed at the cut depth and never a plunge, so the entry guard is untouched.
2. **Cells** (`rest/peel.rs`, `TILE_PER_D = 4`). An area is planned in cells at most 4 tool diameters wide. The neck's one area, which held both mouths and the neck, used to cut one mouth and then the other in every phase, with a retract between.
3. **Travel budget, refused by name** (`rest/budget.rs`, new).
   - Feed out of cut is at most 3.0x the feed in cut, per depth.
   - Retract hops are at most one per rest area after the first, plus the plain Adaptive's `HOP_BUDGET` (8).
   - The yardstick is what the passes remove: a chord is in cut where it clears, on average, at least a graze (0.5% of D) of the rest material planned to be cut. It uses `Raster::cut_count`, new in `raster/conservative.rs`.
   - I did not use the plain Adaptive's `lift::travel` yardstick: it reads wall rides as cut. The old plan scored 402 mm in cut against 194 mm out of cut on it, so a budget on that reading would bind nothing.
   - The figures go into each depth's note.
4. `docs/decisions/2109-rest-adaptive-air.md`: the decision, readings, and what was dropped (lifted returns, chord shortcuts, trimming the run margins, arc fit).

#2108 is not needed: this changes how passes are reached, not what sharp corners or necks get.

## Readings

Debug build, 4 mm tool after a 12 mm tool, two depths. Cut / air feed / rapid are in mm, from the test's independent column stock.

| Fixture | Before | After | Plunges a depth | Planner out/in (one depth) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 40, 3 mm corners | 224 / 967 / 360 | 328 / 562 / 359 | 4 -> 4 | 4.1x -> 2.8x |
| 70 x 50, island, 2 pillars | 250 / 955 / 450 | 388 / 485 / 452 | 4 -> 4 | 4.0x -> 2.6x |
| two bays, 10 mm neck | 954 / 3445 / 1337 | 1438 / 1979 / 545 | 37 -> 10 | 3.6x -> 2.7x |

- **Cut length.** The test's cut figure rises because a retrace rides the wall the last pass left, and that contact reads as cut. On the planner's removal yardstick, in-cut is unchanged (117 / 121 / 467 mm a depth).
- **Moves.** 3216 -> 4064 (corner) and 14850 -> 17840 (neck). The output is still chords; arc fit is not in this PR.
- **Load.** The neck's worst measured load is 15.38% of D, against the planner's own bound of 15.377% (optimal x 1.05, unchanged). Before it read 15.05%. Measured and planner grids are aligned (D/120), so this reading sits right at the planner's limit by design. It is the closest any fixture comes to its `LOAD_SLACK`; please look at this one.

## How tested

Pins:

- `four_corner_residues_...`: air feed at most 2x the cut.
- `an_island_...`: air feed at most 1.5x the cut.
- `a_neck_the_earlier_tool_...`: at most 24 plunges, air feed at most 1.6x the cut.
- `machining2d::adaptive::rest::tests::the_travel_budget_refuses_by_name_past_each_limit` (unit).

Mutations:

- Without the retrace, the corner and neck plans are refused by the budget, and the island fails its air assertion.
- Without the cells, the neck is refused (22 hops against 16).

Gates:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: motion and app suites ok (10.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the final head. Clippy's doc-list lint and an unused test field were fixed after the gate run; `rest_adaptive` and `adaptive::rest` were re-run green on the final head.

## Not exercised

- Run on macOS only.
- The budget was not tried on shapes beyond the fixtures. A real part that travels more is refused by name ("rest Adaptive at Z.. would feed .. mm out of cut .. (over 3.0x) - choose Waterline or Offset rings"). Rest Adaptive is not wired into the Pocket operation until #2033.

Changelog: rest Adaptive reaches each pass back along the one before it and is held to a travel budget (out-of-cut feed at most 3x the cut, one retract per rest area plus 8), refused by name past it (#2109)
Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #2109

**Stacked on #468** (branch `issue/419-thread-dips`, head `d3bb673d`): both change `Script::load`. Only commit `236d40d6` is this issue's work; review that commit. Retarget/refresh after #468 merges.

## What changed (crates/post only)
- Host prelude, rotary and explanation helpers are evaluated separately from user source (`host.js` / `user.cps`), so syntax and runtime errors report the user's own 1-based line and column, with no prelude offset.

A post run is capped at 100,000 output lines counted across hooks; the buffer length is checked in Rust before it is reported or drained, so direct buffer writes cannot slip an oversized program through. Each limit is a named refusal.
- Host prelude moved to `js_host.rs` (re-exported from `js`, public paths unchanged) to keep `js.rs` under 400 lines (386).
- New `post::preview`: `BLANK_TEMPLATE` (original, empty hooks, emits nothing), `DEFAULT_VMC_JSON`, and `SAMPLES` - four deterministic sample streams (facing, contour, pocket, drill) built from committed goldens with setup/operation/tool/spindle/clearance records.

title: test(motion): pin the rest Adaptive raster entry proof and the D/80 load ceiling
body:
**Stacked on #2112** (rest Adaptive, `mkinney:issue/2031-rest-adaptive`, head 71a7fee47). This PR's own change is its last commit (c234093ee); until #2112 merges the diff against main shows #2112's commits too. Merge #2112 first.

## What changed

Tests only (no product code): three pins the M5 review of #2112 found missing.

- **Raster half of the entry proof** - `machining2d::adaptive::rest::tests::the_raster_half_of_the_entry_proof_refuses_on_its_own` (unit test, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/rest/tests.rs`). It hands `Entries` a raster holding a 1 mm pillar that the polygon bound does not hold, then asks for a plunge whose rim would stand 0.2 mm inside the pillar: refused. A plunge clear of the pillar by more than the margin is still proved. Inside the planner the raster comes from the same polygon bound (grown), and the polygon half refuses everything the raster would, so no planner fixture can make the raster refuse on its own. The test therefore works on `Entries` directly.
  - Mutation-checked: removing `&& self.stock.air(p, p, self.footprint)` from `Entries::proved` turns it red, and so does `footprint: 0.0`.
- **Load ceiling on the default D/80 measuring grid** - `on_the_default_measuring_grid_the_load_stays_under_its_documented_ceiling` (`crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`). Optimal x 1.2 (`LOAD_CEILING_D80` in `sim.rs`, with its readings documented), on the climb 3 mm corners and on the conventional 3.5 mm corners with 0.3 mm left.
- **Corner assertion on a fine grid (D/240)** - `on_a_fine_grid_the_corners_read_within_the_planning_margin`. A 26 x 22 pocket with 3.5 mm corners, cut conventionally with 0.3 mm left. On the measuring stock that is 1680 x 1440 cells, under the 4096-cell cap. It must read within the planner's own margin (optimal x 1.05), and every feed stays in the corners.
- `sim.rs`: `Sim::on_grid(region, cell)` and `assert_load_within(reading, slack)`. `assert_load_held` is now `assert_load_within(.., LOAD_SLACK)`.
- `docs/decisions/2113-rest-adaptive-pins.md`.

## Readings (debug, optimal load 14.6% of D)

| Fixture | D/80 | D/120 | D/240 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 40, 3 mm corners, climb | 14.6% | 13.1% | - |

| 26 x 22, 3.5 mm corners, conventional, 0.3 mm left | 14.6% | - | 12.7% |
| two bays, 10 mm neck | 15.0% | 15.0% | - |

No real bug showed up. The D/80 excess is the measuring rim taking in wall in a concave corner: the same paths read lower on finer grids.

title: feat(2d): rest Adaptive planned on proved remaining stock
body:
## What changed

A new generator in the motion crate: `camcraft_motion::machining2d::rest_adaptive(region, params, stock)` - 2D rest machining with the Adaptive strategy, planned on the remaining stock the earlier operations are **proved** to have left. Nothing is assumed cut: no entry bore, no full pocket, no entered previous diameter.

Not stacked. It needs none of #1817's code and merges cleanly with it (checked with `git merge-tree` against `issue/1489-rest-pocket-param` and against main). The Pocket operation's door (`rest2d::rest_strategy`) is untouched and **still refuses Adaptive for rest machining**: the operation only has an entered previous tool, which is no proof. Lifting that refusal belongs to #2033, which produces the `RestStock` this generator reads (the contract is written on #2033).

New code, all under `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/`:

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `rest/stock.rs` | `RestStock`, `StockFloor`: proved floors; the stock and depth guards |
| `rest/entry.rs` | where a plunge is proved clear; the entry guard |
| `rest/peel.rs` | one cut depth: areas, phases, the step ladder, budget, coverage |
| `rest/runs.rs` | the cutting runs: the boundary of the opened room, where it bites |
| `rest/pass.rs` | one pass on trial: legal, crossing-free, walked on the raster, kept or not |
| `rest/leads.rs` | how a pass is reached: stay-down link, or retract and a proved plunge |
| `rest/canon.rs` | the walls as one fixed vertex list (what keeps passes from crossing) |
| `rest/post.rs` | the moves |
| `raster/conservative.rs` | the stock raster read large; proof-of-air and cut queries |

### The contract (the issue's design decision)

- **Separate regions per cut depth**: the legal cutter-center area (pocket less tool radius and stock to leave) and a conservative bound on the material standing at that depth.
- **Stock**: a `StockFloor { z, remaining, uncertain }` claims that inside the pocket, at and above `z`, material stands only in `remaining` or `uncertain`. There is no constructor from a tool diameter.
- **Three guards**, each pinned by a test that runs the planner with that guard off and shows the pin fail:
  - stock - `uncertain` stands as material;
  - depth - a cut depth below every proved floor is refused by name, before anything is planned;
  - entry - a plunge needs the whole footprint plus a margin (0.1 mm or four cells) proved clear by the stock as given, asked of the polygon and of the raster. What this operation's own passes cleared is never credited to a plunge.
- **Conservative raster**: every cell the bound touches stands (the bound is grown by a cell's half diagonal before sampling).
- **Load**: every feed, lead and link included, is walked on that raster before it is kept. No overload fallback.
- **Refused by name**: no proved floor; a cut depth below every proved floor; no entry with proved clearance; a load that cannot be held (with the place); coverage that cannot be proved; a plan past its budget; nothing left to cut.

### The plan

The room is the legal center area minus the material grown by (tool radius - step). It is opened by a disc whose radius falls phase by phase; a pass is the room's boundary where it bites. That gives arcs tangent to both walls in a corner, half loops across a neck, and closed rings round a piece that touches no wall. Passes that ride a wall ride it on one fixed vertex list and retrace the area's earlier way in and out, so the verifier's exact-sign crossing law holds; each candidate is still asked that law. Details, what was tried and dropped, and readings: `docs/decisions/2031-rest-adaptive.md`.

Literature (cited in each module's provenance): Held, LNCS 500 (1991); Yao, Gupta and Nau, CAD 35(9) (2003); Stori and Wright, J. Manuf. Systems 19(3) (2000); Serra, Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology (1982); Otkur and Lazoglu, IJMTM 47 (2007); Altintas, Manufacturing Automation (2012); Hasselgren et al., GPU Gems 2 (2005). No other CAM product's code or output was consulted.

## Readings

4 mm tool after a 12 mm Waterline roughing pass, depths Z-2 and Z-4, optimal load 14.6% of D. "Measured" is `quality::measure` on an independent column stock that the roughing path was cut into.

| Fixture | Passes a depth | Plunges a depth | Worst planned load | Measured | Cut / air feed / rapid (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 40, 3 mm corners | 40 | 4 | 14.4% | 13.1% | 224 / 967 / 360 |
| 70 x 50 with a 14 x 14 island | 36 | 4 | 13.4% | 13.5% | 250 / 955 / 450 |
| two bays, 10 mm neck | 128 | 37 | 15.4% | 15.1% | 954 / 3445 / 1337 |

## How tested

`crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/` (new suite, 9 tests, 36 s wall in debug). `sim.rs` simulates the roughing pass on a column stock, derives the proved stock from it, checks that bound against the simulation, and holds every rest path to: verifier clean; no rapid below the top of the stock except straight up; every plunge down a column the **earlier** operation cleared for the whole footprint; no descent bites; no slotting; the load at each requested depth within 5% of optimal; rest left in reach under 0.05 mm2.

- `four_corner_residues_are_cut_from_proved_stock_within_the_load`
- `a_conventional_cut_leaving_stock_on_the_walls_keeps_every_law`
- `an_island_and_disconnected_rest_areas_are_each_entered_from_proved_space`
- `a_neck_the_earlier_tool_could_not_pass_is_cut_through_within_the_load`
- `a_neck_too_narrow_to_hold_the_load_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_pocket_corner_too_sharp_to_turn_in_within_the_load_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_roughing_pass_that_stops_above_the_rest_floor_is_refused_by_name`
- `stock_that_is_not_proved_is_refused_by_name`
- `degenerate_input_errors_and_never_panics`

Unit tests, `adaptive/rest/tests.rs` (the guard mutations):

- `without_the_stock_guard_a_plunge_lands_in_uncertain_stock`
- `without_the_depth_guard_a_plunge_goes_below_the_proved_floor`
- `without_the_entry_guard_a_plunge_lands_on_material`
- `the_conservative_raster_stands_every_cell_a_sliver_touches`
- `a_wall_stretch_is_walked_on_the_walls_own_vertices`
- `the_phase_radii_fall_gently_and_end_sharp`

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 9916b459d (the code commit): motion suites ok in 418 s (51 binaries and the lib tests), app suites ok in 212 s (47 binaries), 0 failed, wall 10.6 min. The head adds one docs-only commit (`docs/decisions/2031-rest-adaptive.md`) after it. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The three tests the gate names as slow (>60 s) are existing `adaptive_troch` unit tests, not this PR's.

## Known limits, and what was not exercised

- **Sharp pocket corners are refused** (a center arc of 1.0 mm is cut by a 4 mm tool, 0.7 mm is refused, a square corner always is), and so is a **neck under about 2.5 tool diameters**. Both are named refusals with the place, pinned by tests. Follow-up #2108 asks the maintainer what they should get instead.
- **Air feed is about four times the cut length**, and a neck takes 37 plunges a depth. The plain Adaptive's 1.5x budget is not applied. Follow-up #2109.
- **The measured load depends on the measuring grid.** The table and the tests measure on the planner's grid (D/120, the heavy lane's). On the default D/80 grid the same paths read up to 17.4% of D in a concave corner: the yardstick reads on a rim a cell and a half outside the cutter, which stands in more wall on a coarser grid.
- The posted path is chords only (no arc fit): 3216 moves for the corner fixture.

title: feat(geometry): chain 2D sketch primitives into loops with stable ids and nesting
body:
## What changed

New module `camcraft-geometry::sketch_chains` (issue #1861, part of the DXF chain #1452). One call:

```rust
pub fn chain(primitives: &[LayeredPrimitive], options: ChainOptions) -> Result<SketchChains, ChainError>
```

It takes the DXF reader's lines, arcs and circles (#1860, merged as #1937) in millimetres and returns `closed` loops, `open` chains and `rejected` primitives.

- **Joining.** Curve ends within the join tolerance (default 0.01 mm, allowed 1e-5 to 10 mm) are joined, per layer. A wider gap is never bridged: the chain stays open and reports its two free ends. A bridged gap is reported as `max_gap`.
- **Arc metadata survives.** A chain segment is the input primitive turned to the walk direction (`reversed`, start angle and sweep sign rewritten). Nothing is flattened or snapped.
- **Stable `ChainId`.** Closed loops are walked counterclockwise from their lowest joint, open chains from their lower end. The id is the 128-bit FNV-1a hash of the layer name and the curves in that order, quantized to 1e-6 mm. It does not depend on draw order or direction.
- **Outer or hole.** Depth is counted by an exact crossing-number test against the arcs. Even depth is `Outer`, odd is `Hole`, with the innermost container as `parent`. This is the even-odd rule of `geo2d::Region`.
- **Named refusals, per chain.** `DuplicatePrimitive`, `DegenerateSegment`, `Branch { at, degree }`, `SelfCrossing { at }`, `ZeroArea`, `DuplicateChain`. Closed chains that cross or touch each other keep their geometry but get `NestingAmbiguous` instead of a role, and so does every loop inside one of them. `SketchChains::strict()` turns the first of these into an `Err`.
- **Hard errors.** A bad tolerance, a non-finite, out-of-range or invalid primitive, and a drawing over the limits (coordinates below 1e7 mm, 2,000,000 primitives, 200,000,000 pair tests) return `Err`. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the module.

No new dependency, no file I/O, no ECS. No user-facing command is added, so there is no MCP tool in this PR; the import command and its tool are #1862.

## Algorithms and sources (clean room)

| Step | Source |
|---|---|
| End clustering on a grid | Bentley, Stanat and Williams, 1977 |
| Clusters and components | Tarjan, union-find, 1975 |
| Identity hash | FNV-1a, IETF draft-eastlake-fnv |
| Candidate pairs for the crossing search | Sweep and prune: Cohen, Lin, Manocha and Ponamgi, 1995; axis choice from Ericson, 2005 |
| Segment, line-circle and circle-circle contacts | O'Rourke, 1998; Schneider and Eberly, 2003 |
| Containment | Crossing number: Shimrat, 1962; Haines, 1994 |
| Loop area with arcs | Green's theorem |

Each submodule carries its provenance line. No vendor code, file or output was consulted. Decisions, alternatives dropped and known limits are in `docs/decisions/1861-sketch-chaining.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green, 10 steps, 0 failed, 30.2 min (head 3c65e18a2). A geometry change makes quick run the batch plan, so that is every debug suite plus clippy.

Pinning tests, 18 in three new suites under `crates/geometry/tests/`:

- `sketch_chains.rs`
  - `unordered_lines_chain_into_one_counterclockwise_loop`
  - `chain_id_ignores_draw_order_and_direction_but_not_layer_or_geometry` (pins the id value; I recomputed it independently outside Rust)
  - `arc_metadata_survives_chaining`
  - `gap_wider_than_tolerance_stays_open_and_is_reported`
  - `open_chain_of_lines_and_arcs_starts_at_its_lower_end`
  - `arcs_that_close_a_circle_and_tangent_fillets_are_clean_loops`
  - `dxf_polyline_bulges_and_circles_chain_with_their_arcs` (through `dxf::parse`; same id as the loose primitives)
- `sketch_chains_nesting.rs`
  - `nested_rectangles_and_circles_classify_as_outer_and_hole` (compared with `geo2d::Region`)
  - `containment_follows_the_arcs_not_their_chords`
  - `shuffled_nests_of_mixed_shapes_keep_their_depth_and_parent` (200 seeded nests, rotated, shuffled, flipped)
  - `long_loop_chains_in_bounded_time` (40,000-side loop; 50,000-segment tall strip that pins the sweep axis)
- `sketch_chains_refusals.rs`
  - `self_crossing_loop_is_refused_by_name`
  - `branching_vertex_is_a_named_diagnostic`
  - `degenerate_pieces_are_refused_by_name`
  - `invalid_input_is_an_error_not_a_panic`
  - `crossing_loops_get_no_outer_or_hole_reading`
  - `dense_drawing_is_refused_within_the_work_limit`
  - `random_grid_sketches_never_panic_and_do_not_depend_on_input_order` (400 seeded sketches; every primitive chained or rejected once; depth checked against flattened polygons; accepted loops pass `Region::new`)

## What was not exercised

- No real-world DXF file was chained; inputs are hand-built or generated, plus one DXF text through the reader.
- Two curves that meet at a tangent cusp can read as `SelfCrossing` when rounding makes them cross away from the joint. Fillets and S-curves are pinned as clean; the cusp case is not.
- Open chains are not tested for self-crossing, by decision.
- Nothing calls `chain()` yet: the ECS entity, the project file and the import command are #1862.
- Debug-build timing only; the release lanes were not run.

Process change: no

Changelog: Sketch chaining in camcraft-geometry: DXF lines, arcs and circles join within a tolerance into closed loops and open chains with stable ids, arcs kept analytic, outer-versus-hole nesting, and named refusals for branches, self-crossing loops and degenerate pieces (#1861)

## What changed

- Interpret C rotary `"axis": [0, 0, -1]` as clockwise about `+Z` (`-1.0`) and `[0, 0, 1]` or unstated as `+Z` (`+1.0`).
- Add `AxisLimits::c_z_sense`, `AxisLimits::c_program_travel`, `Machine::c_axis`, and `Machine::reversed_c_rotary` in `crates/post/src/machine/direction.rs`.

title: fix(sim): credit bounded 3D edge-break volumes
body:
## What changed

Stock verification now credits framed 3D edge-break volumes.
The records describe flat bisector chamfers, concave ball arcs, and convex rounded profiles.
Each segment carries an orthonormal outward bisector frame.
The verifier credits only declared material connected to the model surface.
Cuts outside the cap or below its profile still convict as gouges.

The existing #529 operation-width bound still applies.
Framed depth cannot exceed framed width.
Invalid dimensions, frames, and profiles drop the record with a diagnostic.
Project loading preserves valid profiles and full-precision framed endpoints.
Tilted work frames rotate the cap directions with the edge.
Existing Chamfer2D and v1 Deburr records retain their cone law and wire shape.
Framed records require a zero slope so older readers discard them safely.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1891-edge-break-volumes.md`.
The branch starts at upstream/main `a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504`.

## Cause

EdgeBreak described only a vertical cone.
Simulation measured its reach in XY.
That model cannot describe vertical or oblique bisector caps or circular break profiles.

## Tests

The initial runtime pin `a_framed_break_survives_the_project_record_reader` failed on unchanged upstream code.
The reader loaded zero records instead of one.
The pin passes with this change.

The additional runtime pin `tiny_circle_direction_rates_do_not_underflow_into_extra_credit` caught an underflow in the first implementation.
Normalizing the circle calculation fixes it.
Restoring the old calculation reproduces the failure.

All 21 new pins pass.
All 8 legacy edge-break pins pass.

- CL `edge_volume` has 9 pins for finite caps, circle profiles, vertical and oblique edges, tiny rates, connected intervals, corrupt frames, rotation, and legacy cones.
- Sim `edge_volume_credit` has 4 pins for valid profiles and multiple passes, vertical and oblique credit, real gouges, detached caps, malformed records, and mismatched lattices.
- App `edge_volume_bound` has 2 pins for operation width/kind bounds and corrupt-frame/excess-depth refusal.
- App `project::break_dto::volume_tests` has 5 pins for loading, legacy bytes, profiles, malformed extensions, and precise endpoints.
- App `a_framed_cap_verifies_after_loading_but_a_deeper_or_forged_cut_convicts` checks real stock verification, project save/load, deeper cuts, inflated depth, and jointly forged width/depth.

All 26 mutations produced runtime failures and passed after restoration.
Old upstream sanity, simulation credit, and project-reader implementations were restored for the baseline checks.
The project-reader baseline retained only the new field plumbing needed to compile.

- framed-slope-zero; legacy-width-finite; framed-depth-bound; segment-frame-count: red, restored green.
- radius-finite; radius-half-width; radius-sag-depth; finite-span-size: red, restored green.
- unit-outward; unit-across; frame-normal-orthogonal; outward-tangent-orthogonal; across-tangent-orthogonal: red, restored green.
- connected-only; longitudinal-end-planes; cross-width-planes; inward-depth-planes: red, restored green.
- concave-circle-profile; convex-circle-profile; analytic-circle-crossings; stable-circle-sag: red, restored green.
- tilted-frame-rotation; upstream-sanity-method; upstream-sim-credit; upstream-project-reader; normalized-circle-rates: red, restored green.

The shared CL change triggered the existing batch fallback.

No retry was needed.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` also passed.
Effort: max, with no escalation.

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised

- Supported revolved spun half-profiles (`CENTRELINE`/`AXIS` around `+Z`, convertible with `#743` `SpunProfile`) and extruded closed 2D contours along `X`/`Y`/`Z` with positive depth.
- Preserved raw STEP bytes in ECS `StepSource`, `.camproj` (`EntityDto.step_source`), and `.camfixtures` (`FixtureEntry.step_source`), never converting imported STEP fixtures into profiles on import.
- Added undoable commands `InsertProfileFixture`, `SetFixtureProfile`, and `DeriveFixtureProfile`, plus five MCP tools in `crates/app/src/mcp/fixture_profile_tools.rs`.
- `DeriveFixtureProfile` and `derive_fixture_profile` derive a reference profile only from a STEP fixture. They refuse, by name, a DXF/profile fixture and an imported mesh fixture without a STEP source. Thus the profile that defines the steel stays the collision bound.
- Added the `"Add DXF / profile…"` dialog and per-row edit/derive/DXF-export controls in `crates/ui`, keeping `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_menu.rs` untouched.
- Added decision record `docs/decisions/744-fixture-profiles.md`.

## Cause

Turning chucks, jaws, collets, vises, parallels, and step blocks lacked parametric 2D profile authoring, DXF import/export, and post-placement profile editing. Vendor STEP fixtures needed to keep their raw STEP geometry intact rather than being replaced by approximated profiles.

## Tests

Pins:
- `camcraft-geometry --test dxf_profile`: `spun_fixture_imports_from_dxf_centreline_plus_half_profile_and_roundtrips`, `extruded_fixture_reads_closed_profile_and_depth_from_annotation_or_arg`, `dxf_profile_malformed_inputs_give_named_errors_never_panic` (3 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test fixture_profiles`: `spun_dxf_fixture_imports_meshes_edits_and_roundtrips`, `extruded_vise_jaw_from_dxf_is_hit_by_rapid_until_edited_below_it`, `step_fixture_can_optionally_derive_profile_while_keeping_step_as_source`, `profile_fixture_roundtrips_library_and_malformed_project_key_loads_safely` (4 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test fixture_step_library`: `step_fixture_saves_to_library_as_step_and_reinserts_unchanged` (1 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_fixture_profile`: `mcp_fixture_profile_workflow_imports_edits_exports_and_keeps_step`, `mcp_derive_fixture_profile_refuses_generated_fixture_and_keeps_its_profile` (2 passed).
- `camcraft-app --test fixture_profile_collision`: `generated_fixture_refuses_reference_derivation_and_keeps_its_collision_bound`, `mesh_fixture_without_step_source_refuses_reference_derivation`, plus the 4 earlier collision tests (6 passed).
- `camcraft-ui --lib egui_app::fixture_profile_tests`: `fixtures_page_button_opens_profile_dialog_and_inserts_dxf_fixtures`, `refused_profile_or_bad_dxf_is_named_in_dialog`, `editing_placed_profile_row_regenerates_mesh_and_exports_dxf`, `step_fixture_keeps_raw_step_and_allows_reference_derive_only` (4 passed inside 852 lib tests).

Mutation checks:
- Weakened `dxf_profile::resolve_depth` positive-depth guard (`> 0.0`): `dxf_profile_malformed_inputs_give_named_errors_never_panic` failed red, restored and passed green.
- Disabled `SetFixtureProfile::new` STEP-source guard in `profile_fixture.rs`: `mcp_fixture_profile_workflow_imports_edits_exports_and_keeps_step` failed red, restored and passed green.
- Cleared `ImportModel::apply` `step_source::set` write in `import_model.rs`: `step_fixture_saves_to_library_as_step_and_reinserts_unchanged` failed red, restored and passed green.
- Disabled the STEP-source guard in `target_fixture` (`profile_fixture.rs`): both new `fixture_profile_collision` tests and `mcp_derive_fixture_profile_refuses_generated_fixture_and_keeps_its_profile` failed red, restored and passed green.

## Goldens moved

none (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- `camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting::troubleshooting_messages_still_exist_in_the_sources` failed because `base-2077` predates `upstream/main` commit `92430ff0` (`#2051`); our branch made no change to troubleshooting strings and passes once merged with `main`.
- `gate quick` steps `geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, and `motion` passed prior to server restart (`quick-20261116-012138`); `ui`, workspace `clippy -D warnings`, and all other `app` suites passed in `quick-20261116-015550`.
- Native OS modal file-picker interaction and wasm32 browser target were not executed in headless mode (tested via `load_profile_dxf_bytes`, `CommandKind::ExportFixtureDxf`, and `browser_files` guards).

## Overlaps

- `#2077` (base of this stack): touches `schema.rs`, `commands/delete_entity.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`, `lib.rs`, `mcp/tools.rs`, `project/{apply,entity,wire}.rs`, `egui_app/mod.rs`, and `state.rs` in different fields/variants; merge `#2077` first.
- `#2092`: touches `schema.rs`, `mcp/tools.rs`, and `project/{apply,validate,wire}.rs` in different fields and functions; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2024`: touches `commands/update_model.rs` and `project/{apply,entity,validate}.rs` in different fields (`mesh_open` vs `step_source`); whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#1687`: left `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_menu.rs` untouched to avoid conflicting.

title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `camcraft-geometry::dxf_writer`: `write_and_parse_round_trip_lines_arcs_circles_layers_and_units`, `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name` (2 passed).
  - `camcraft-tools::spun::envelope::tests::thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile` (6 passed): `step_to_dxf_half_profile_envelops_every_sampled_mesh_point`, `non_revolved_step_or_fine_32_plus_band_mesh_is_conservatively_enveloped`, `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`, `dxf_half_profile_import_with_lines_and_arcs_lands_as_tool_body`, `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`, `round_trip_step_to_dxf_to_body_to_dxf_is_stable_within_tolerance`.
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile_mcp`: `mcp_holder_dxf_and_step_profile_tools_list_round_trip_undo_and_refuse` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-ui::egui_app::tests::tool_profile` (9 passed, adding `profile_tab_states_conservative_envelope_and_half_profile_rules_and_dxf_workflow` and `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`).
- Mutations (each tested red after weakening the guard and green after restore):
  - `spun_envelope::join` `max(r)` -> `min(r)`: failed `thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile`; restored green.
  - `dxf::writer` zero-length `LINE` guard bypassed: failed `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name`; restored green.
  - `tool_profile_dxf_import` centreline-crossing guard bypassed: failed `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`; restored green.
  - `step_to_spun_profile` ISO 13399 requirement replaced with `+Z` fallback: failed `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`; restored green.
  - `convert_body_draft_to_profile` clear-axis check bypassed: failed `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`; restored green.
- Gate:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` expanded to the `batch` tier (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/mod.rs` is a shared crate) and passed all 10 steps in 39.8 min with 0 failures (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, `ui`, `clippy -D warnings`).

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Native OS file-picker modal calls (`import_profile_dxf_dialog`, `export_profile_dxf_dialog`, `import_step_profile_dialog`) delegate to desktop `rfd`; headless UI tests exercise `import_profile_dxf_from`, `export_profile_dxf_to`, `import_step_profile_from`, and `Convert to profile`.
- Release-tier `SLOW_BINARIES` (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`) were outside the `batch` gate run.

## Overlaps

- `#2092` (stacked on `#2054`) edits different functions in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs` (`library_body`, `SetToolBody::spun`), `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs` (`sync_tool_profile_ui`, `pick_library_holder`, `run_set_tool_holder`, `editor_library_holder`), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` (lines 84-87), and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` (lines 32, 38, 281); this PR uses `tool_body::build_spun` (no `ToolBody` struct literals) and companion modules/tail blocks; whichever merges second refreshes.

- `#2077` edits `crates/app/src/lib.rs` line 118 and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` line 281, different lines from our additions at `lib.rs` and the tail of `all()` in `mcp/tools.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.

Rendered with the real egui shell harness at 1600 × 1200. Before uses the exact `upstream/main` (`a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504`) Profile and Body page sources. title: fix(ui): disable X/Y WCS tilt on milling setups and point to Part alignment
body:
Stacked on #1684 (merge #1684 first)

## What changed

- Added Option 1 (Slice 1) milling guard in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`.
- On `Kind::Mill` setups (`machine::kind_of(&state.world) == Kind::Mill`), `origin_fields` disables the `Tilt about X (roll)` and `Tilt about Y (pitch)` spinbuttons and shows a hint pointing to `Part alignment` on the Setup page.
- `quarter_turns` renders the 3x2 turn buttons via `turn_row`, disabling `Turn X+`, `Turn X-`, `Turn Y+`, and `Turn Y-` on milling setups with the same hover hint.
- `X origin`, `Y origin`, `Z origin`, `Turn about Z (yaw)`, `Turn Z+`, `Turn Z-`, `Level`, and `Set Origin` stay live on milling setups.
- When an existing milling WCS is already tilted (`setup_wcs_tilt::setup_problem`), `wcs_page` warns that generation will refuse it and instructs the user to click `Level` and use `Part alignment`.
- Non-mill machines (such as `Kind::Lathe`) keep X/Y tilt spinbuttons and all six quarter-turn buttons live.
- Recorded the Option 1 choice and deferred items in `docs/decisions/1542-milling-wcs-tilt-guard.md`.

## Cause

Milling generation refuses any WCS tilted off machine Z (`setup_wcs_tilt`), while the WCS page still invited users to tilt milling WCS axes via `Tilt about X (roll)`, `Tilt about Y (pitch)`, and X/Y quarter turns instead of using `Part alignment`.

## Tests

- Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs`:
  - `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment`: red before fix (`Tilt about X (roll) must be disabled on a milling setup`), green after fix.
  - `non_mill_setup_keeps_xy_wcs_tilt_and_turns_live`: verifies `Tilt about X/Y` spinbuttons and all 6 turn buttons stay live and `Turn X+` tilts the WCS on `Kind::Lathe`.
  - Updated `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane` so `Turn Z+`/`Turn Z-` are asserted live and `Turn X±`/`Turn Y±` disabled on `with_stock()` (`Kind::Mill`), keeping equal-size and alignment assertions intact.
- Mutation checks on `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`:
  - Reverted to `base-1684`: `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment` (`Tilt about X (roll)`) and `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane` (`Turn X+`) both failed; green after restore.
  - Forced `turn_row` `enabled = true` and `tilted_mill = false`: both tests failed on `Turn X+`; green after restore.
  - Forced `tilted_mill = false` alone: `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment` failed missing the tilted-WCS warning; green after restore.
- Gate and lint:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`14s`, `ui suites`: `ui lib`, `ui:boundary`, `ui:boundary_picks`, `ui:sinker_setup`, `ui:theme_files`, 0 failed).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- Full cross-workspace gate beyond `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (only `crates/ui` code changed).
- Feature-pick Z-tilt guard (`wcs_pick_row.rs`) and MCP `set_wcs` milling guard (Slice 2, deferred because `#1931` is relocating `wcs_pick_row.rs`; `setup_wcs_tilt` continues to block tilted milling setups at generation).

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #1684 (`quarter_turns`, `turn_wcs`, and `wcs_page_tests.rs`); merge #1684 first, then retarget or refresh this PR.
- Touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs` alongside #1717 (`OFFSET_GROUP`, different functions/lines) and #1738 (`flip_row` inside `quarter_turns` between `Turn X-` and `Level`; this PR leaves widget placement between `Turn X-` and `Level` unchanged). Whichever merges later refreshes.

title: fix(2d): add 2D shape-mask verifier and PNG diff reporter
body:
## What changed

Added a test-only 2D toolpath shape-mask verifier under `crates/motion/tests/common/` and a pure-Rust RGB difference PNG writer with no new dependencies. The helper checks overcut, leftover, progressive rim engagement, symmetry and stock extension. Added helper regressions and generator fixtures for Adaptive and trochoidal paths. Updated the testing instructions and decision record.

Ramps contribute only their selected depth interval. Clearance records the deepest actual cutter position covering each cell. A descending helix never clears its entire footprint at its endpoint depth.

The two radial-engagement fixtures explicitly start with a predrilled 8 mm radius bore at their final floor: Adaptive at `(0, 0, -5)`, trochoidal at `(-20, 0, -6)`. The radius is the 3 mm entry orbit plus the 5 mm cutter radius. Initial stock clearance is bounded by that region and depth. It gives no swept-path coverage credit. The generated paths still must pass their original overcut, leftover, symmetry and stock-extension checks. Engagement bounds are unchanged.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test shape_masks --test trochoid_slot --test adaptive_hsm`: 11 helper tests passed, 12 trochoidal tests passed, 2 Adaptive tests passed and 5 heavy tests stayed ignored.
- Adaptive measured maximum cut width: 1.956193 mm against a 2.352 mm limit. Trochoidal: 5.218097 mm against a 5.375 mm limit.
- Pin: `shape_mask_precleared_bore_respects_its_radius_and_depth` accepts light side cutting with the stated bore, rejects a smaller or shallower bore, rejects overload outside it, and confirms initial stock does not credit generated swept coverage. The existing solid-stock ramp and helix regressions still pass.
- Isolated mutations: disabling precleared initialization failed the new pin (2.000 mm > 0.688 mm); reverting the Adaptive fixture to solid stock failed its generator pin (10.000 mm > 2.352 mm); reverting the trochoidal fixture failed its generator pin (10.000 mm > 5.375 mm). Each restored pin passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,033 passed, 0 failed, 53 ignored across 86 motion test binaries (library plus 85 integration suites).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.

No runtime CAM code, dependencies, goldens, screenshots or review evidence changed. Difference PNGs are temporary failure artifacts and are not committed. Heavy ignored tests and GUI suites were not run.

Process change: yes
Changelog: add test-only 2D toolpath shape-mask verifier and RGB diff PNG reporter
Fixes #1768

title: fix(ui): give painted browser rows and menus AccessKit labels
body:
Stacked on #2027 (merge #2027 first)

## What changed

- Added AccessKit `WidgetInfo` labels to painted browser tree rows (`"Browser: {label}"`) and eye toggles (`"{Hide|Show} {label}"`) in `painted.rs`.
- Clamped the browser tree rect width in `browser_pane::browser` to the visible clip edge.
- Added AccessKit `WidgetInfo` labels to every context-menu row in `tree_menu.rs`, using `WidgetType::Button` for items and `WidgetType::Label` with `Sense::hover()` for headers.
- Filtered `"Browser: "` nodes out of `setups_declutter::shows` so persistent browser rows do not collide with Setup page label assertions.
- Removed `BROWSER_TREE_TOP` and `BROWSER_EYE_X` from `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`.
- Rewrote all six browser behaviour tests to locate rows, eyes, and menu items by label instead of fixed coordinates, and recorded the design choice in `docs/decisions/1989-browser-tree-accesskit.md`.

## Cause

Painted browser rows, eye toggles, and tree context-menu rows drew with `ui.interact` and `Painter` without attaching `WidgetInfo`. Tests had to calculate pixel coordinates with `BROWSER_TREE_TOP` and `BROWSER_EYE_X`. In `browser_pane::browser`, the top button strip inside `egui_dock`'s `ScrollArea` also widened `ui.available_width()` past `ui.clip_rect().right()`, placing the `Stock` eye center outside its clipped `interact_rect` so AccessKit clicks missed it.

## Tests

All six rewritten tests failed on `base-2027` before the fix and pass after it:
- `stock_eye_hides_the_viewport_stock_without_removing_it_from_the_document`
- `dragging_an_operation_row_reorders_within_global_setup`
- `operations_heading_menu_pastes_the_copied_operation`
- `operation_type_menu_requires_confirmation`
- `operation_menu_suppresses_and_sets_the_after_action`
- `program_entry::the_operation_menu_adds_an_entry_and_its_own_menu_edits_it`

Mutation checks against `base-2027`:
- Reverting `painted.rs` made `stock_eye_hides_the_viewport_stock_without_removing_it_from_the_document` and `dragging_an_operation_row_reorders_within_global_setup` fail; restoring it made both pass.
- Reverting `browser_pane.rs` made `stock_eye_hides_the_viewport_stock_without_removing_it_from_the_document` fail; restoring it made it pass.

title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

## Notes for the reviewer

- A build of main between #1453 and this change reads v62 and would drop the `holder` key (development builds only; v0.21.0 refuses v62).
- A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it. A copy kept the old numbers.
- The tool record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten by the entry (they are what the tool goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move the stamp). The settings show the entry's numbers.

Changelog: A tool's library holder is stored as a reference to the library entry (name, gauge length, projection) in the project and tool library files, not as a drawn copy; the tool settings show the entry's holder size. Breaking: v0.21.0 and older refuse a file that names a library holder.

Effort: max (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a project or tool library saved with a library holder states it as a reference (project v62, `.camtools` version 2); v0.21.0 and older refuse such a file.

Process change: yes

Fixes #2016

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAAAJyAPrC37zBzbbX

## UI screenshots

These images show the seeded `EM-0600-4FL` tool with the `BT30 ER20` holder.

title: fix(ui): read status strip, ribbon tabs, window margin and drop hint from theme
body:
Stacked on #2027 (merge #2027 first)

## What changed

- Added five geometry tokens to `theme::Tokens` (`window_margin`, `status_h`, `ribbon_tab_pad_x`, `ribbon_tab_gap`, `ribbon_tab_stroke`) and `clamp::RADIUS_WINDOW` (`24`).
- Updated `Tokens::DARK` and `Tokens::LIGHT` in `theme/tables.rs` with defaults that preserve existing dark and light pixel geometry (`6.0`, `22.0`, `12.0`, `2.0`, `2.0`).
- Added `theme::status_h(t)` to return the maximum of `t.status_h`, `t.control_height + 4.0`, and `t.font_row * 1.3 + 4.0`.
- Wired `Tokens::style()` to read `spacing.window_margin` from `self.window_margin` instead of `item_spacing_y.max(6.0)`.
- Wired `shell::shell_layout` to size the bottom status bar with `theme::status_h(&pal)`.
- Wired `panes::ribbon_tabs` to read left inset from `pal.item_spacing_x`, tab padding from `pal.ribbon_tab_pad_x`, inter-tab gap from `pal.ribbon_tab_gap`, and underline stroke from `pal.ribbon_tab_stroke`.
- Wired `file_drop::paint_hint` to read border inset from `pal.window_margin`, corner radius from `pal.radius_window`, and stroke thickness and text size from `pal.font_label`.
- Split `theme_files::names` into `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme_files/names.rs` to keep every file under 400 lines.
- Added `docs/decisions/2064-theme-shell-metrics.md`.

## Cause

Shell metrics for window margin, bottom status height, ribbon tab spacing and stroke, and the file drop hint used hardcoded constants or `item_spacing_y` instead of dedicated theme tokens.

## Tests

All five pinning tests failed before the fix on unchanged `base-2027` and pass after the final edit:

- `theme_shell_metrics::window_margin_comes_from_own_token_not_item_spacing`
- `theme_shell_metrics::status_h_and_ribbon_tab_keys_parse_and_clamp`
- `egui_app::tests::ribbon_rows::issue_2064_pins::status_strip_height_tracks_theme_controls_and_status_h`
- `egui_app::tests::ribbon_rows::issue_2064_pins::ribbon_tabs_follow_theme_spacing_pad_gap_and_stroke`
- `egui_app::tests::file_drop::issue_2064_pins::drop_hint_reads_window_margin_radius_and_font_from_theme`

Mutation checks (each reverted or loosened code path failed red, then passed green after restoring):

1. `theme.rs` `Tokens::style()` `window_margin` reverted to `item_spacing_y.max(6.0)` -> `window_margin_comes_from_own_token_not_item_spacing` failed, restored passed.
2. `theme_files/overlay.rs` clamps on the 5 new keys loosened -> `status_h_and_ribbon_tab_keys_parse_and_clamp` failed, restored passed.
3. `theme.rs` `status_h()` stripped to `t.status_h` -> `status_strip_height_tracks_theme_controls_and_status_h` failed, restored passed.
4. `shell.rs` `.exact_size(22.0)`, `panes.rs` `ribbon_tabs` literals, and `file_drop.rs` `paint_hint` literals reverted -> all 3 `issue_2064_pins` tests failed, restored passed.

Gate and lint after final edit:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed (`ui lib` 832 passed / 6 ignored, `boundary` 3, `boundary_picks` 6, `sinker_setup` 2, `theme_files` 14, `theme_shell_metrics` 2, `waterjet_tool` 1; 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with zero warnings.

## Goldens moved

None (`0` `.nc`, `.cl`, or `.png` files changed).

## Not exercised

- `assets/themes/theme.json.example` was not updated here because #2038 creates that file on top of #2027 and this branch stacks one level on #2027.
- Unchanged non-UI workspace crates and Windows-made pixel snapshot goldens did not run in the quick gate.

## Overlaps

- `#2027` (stacked on it; merge `#2027` first): modifies `theme.rs` (`Tokens`, `clamp`, `geom_legal`), `theme/tables.rs`, `theme_files.rs` (`names`, `COLOR_NAMES`, `GEOM_NAMES`), `theme_files/overlay.rs` (`apply_overlay`), `shell.rs` (constants above `STATUS_H`), `panes.rs` (`ribbon_tabs`), and `tests/ribbon_rows.rs`.
- `#2029`, `#2023`, `#1798`, `#1330` touch other functions in `shell.rs`; `#1798` touches other functions in `panes.rs`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Read status strip height, ribbon tab metrics, window margin, and drop hint geometry from theme tokens
Fixes #2064

## Review screenshots

These screenshots show the actual shell, tool editor, and file drop hint.
The renderer uses `egui_kittest` and the actual `View3D` GPU output at 1440 × 960 pixels.
The ribbon and status images are crops of that output.

Both runs use the same dark theme and scene.
The theme sets `window_margin=20`, `status_h=48`, `ribbon_tab_pad_x=24`, `ribbon_tab_gap=12`, and `ribbon_tab_stroke=6`.
It also sets `item_spacing_x=16`, `radius_window=20`, and `font_label=15`.
These values make the changed behavior visible. The default values preserve the previous geometry.

The after run uses the consumers at `bacb784b0207c43ea610bb8da9c8beb15f9ba61b`.
For the before run, the temporary harness restores the parent ribbon tab function, status height, window margin expression, and drop hint body.
The before run keeps the new token schema to load the same theme file.
It keeps an unused palette argument on the drop hint function so the harness compiles.
Thus, the before run shows the parent consumer behavior with the same theme configuration.
It does not use an unchanged parent checkout.

camcraft-ui - a CAM program that turns 3D models into NC programs

  --version

## What changed

- `painted::caption` reads `pal.font_caption` instead of `MIN_LABEL_PX`.

- `Tokens::DARK.font_caption` and `Tokens::LIGHT.font_caption` change from `12.5` to `10.0` so captions fit inside `ribbon_caption_row_h` (`18.0` px) and stay smaller than `font_label` (`11.0` px).
- `ribbon_rows` tests track `t.font_caption` and pin the token, the clamp window, and built-in theme fit.
- Added `docs/decisions/2063-font-caption.md`.

## Cause

Commit `33cd8b56` raised `Tokens::font_caption` to `12.5` when it removed `painted::caption`. Commit `e5fcf588` restored `painted::caption` with `FontId::proportional(MIN_LABEL_PX)` (`10.0`). Later work lowered `font_label` to `11.0`, leaving `font_caption` unused at `12.5`.

## Tests

- Pins (`ribbon_rows`): `caption_uses_font_caption_token`, `caption_clamps_out_of_range_font_caption`, `builtin_caption_font_fits_caption_row`, and updated `tab_text_and_caption_text_fit_their_rows_in_each_theme` failed on unchanged code (`10.0 != 16.0`, `10.0 != 6.0`, `12.5 px` overflowed `18 px`) and passed after the fix (`8 passed; 0 failed`).

  1. Reverted `painted.rs` to `#2027` (`MIN_LABEL_PX`): `caption_uses_font_caption_token` and `caption_clamps_out_of_range_font_caption` failed. Restored `painted.rs`: passed.
  2. Removed `clamp::range` in `painted.rs` (raw `pal.font_caption`): `caption_clamps_out_of_range_font_caption` failed. Restored `clamp::range`: passed.
  3. Reverted `tables.rs` to `#2027` (`12.5`): `builtin_caption_font_fits_caption_row` and `tab_text_and_caption_text_fit_their_rows_in_each_theme` failed. Restored `10.0`: passed.
- Structural check: `ribbon_labels_whole_and_captions_painted` passed (`1 passed; 0 failed`).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed (`ui suites`: `--lib` `832 passed, 6 ignored`, `boundary` `3 passed`, `boundary_picks` `6 passed`, `sinker_setup` `2 passed`, `theme_files` `14 passed`, `waterjet_tool` `1 passed`).
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed with zero warnings.

## Goldens moved

None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Full workspace `cargo xtask gate` outside `camcraft-ui`.
- `#[ignore]` visual snapshot tests (6 ignored in `--lib`).
- Interactive live window rendering with a custom `"font_caption"` JSON theme file (`painted::caption` runs headless via `egui_kittest::Harness`).

## Overlaps

- PR #2027 (stacked on #2027; merge #2027 first): touches `painted::caption` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs`, `Tokens::DARK` and `Tokens::LIGHT` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme/tables.rs`, and `tab_text_and_caption_text_fit_their_rows_in_each_theme` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ribbon_rows.rs`.
