title: fix(import): stop a STEP pass after a few runaway faces
body:
## What changed

- All face meters and edge-curve meters of one shell pass share one pass budget (`Pass`, new `step_meter.rs`).
- Each meter counts its first refusal in the pass one time. A refusal is a cap that ran out, a division that did not converge, or a boundary-search fault.
- At `PASS_TRIPS` (3) trips the pass stops. Then each meter answers its fixed point, and each face in flight ends within one sweep.
- The stopped pass is refused by name. The refusal names the first face or edge that really tripped. It adds: "the tessellation stopped after 3 faces or edges ran out of evaluations; more of the model may be broken".
- A stopped pass is never "continuous". Thus no coarser mesh is kept for it.
- A meter that the stop cut short is not a trip. Its `exhaust` and its search faults are not recorded. Thus a refusal never names a healthy face.
- `Meter` moved from `step_guard.rs` to `step_meter.rs`. This keeps `step_guard.rs` under 400 lines (now 365).

## Cause

The 150 M evaluation cap applied to each face, not to the pass. Each runaway face spent a full cap (10-15 s) before it tripped. A file with N runaway faces thus cost N caps divided by the core count.

## Tests

Pins (red before the fix: yes):

- `step_meter::tests::a_pass_with_many_runaway_faces_stops_after_a_few_trips`. A shell with 31 runaway faces. Before: `31 runaway faces spent 6200175 evaluations, bound 2200011`. After: under the bound (3 caps plus one cap for each worker thread).
- `import_step_guard::a_shell_of_many_runaway_faces_is_refused_after_a_few_trips`. End to end: `bspline_discontinuous.step` with face #53 listed 40 more times. It is refused by name, and the refusal says that the pass stopped.
- `step_meter::tests::the_pass_stops_at_the_trip_limit_and_a_stopped_meter_is_not_a_trip`
- `step_meter::tests::a_stopped_pass_of_proven_faces_is_not_continuous`
- `step_meter::tests::edge_trips_count_against_the_pass_budget`
- `step_meter::tests::the_refusal_of_a_stopped_pass_says_it_stopped`
- `step_meter::tests::a_pass_with_one_runaway_face_is_not_stopped` (unchanged behaviour below the limit)

Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pins were run, and the code was restored:

- `spend` ignores a stopped pass: red.
- `spend_many` ignores a stopped pass: red.
- A stopped pass can be continuous: red.
- `exhaust` on a stopped pass: red.
- `flag` on a stopped pass: red.
- Faces do not share the pass (the old code): red (4 pins).
- Edges do not share the pass: red.
- The refusal has no stop note: red.
- The pass is not reset between passes: red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (lib plus 18 import suites, 78 s). These include `step_fidelity`, `large_models`, `model_fidelity`, `step_budget` and `import_step_guard_default_cap`. Healthy imports did not change. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The release heavy lanes (the measured corpus and the 150 M default-cap timing in release).
- The kernel crate's test copy of the guard (`crates/kernel/tests/step_util/truck_guard.rs`). It is a separate test helper and this PR does not change it.

## Overlaps

None in substance. Open PR #1738 lists these files only because of the drift of its stacked base. It does not change the STEP guard.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1599-pass-eval-budget.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: STEP import stops a shell's tessellation pass after 3 faces or edges run out of evaluations, so a file with many broken faces is refused by name in bounded time (#1599)

Fixes #1599

title: feat(turning): lathe chucks fit to the stock in the dialog, inside grip, stepped jaws
body:
First slice of #1468. Fork synced from `upstream/main` at 31f8d03d7 (branch cut from it, not from a tag). Not stacked: no open PR changes these files except the camcraft-mcp skill (#1738, #1817, #2037 edit other rows).

## What changed

- **Dialog: "Fit to the stock" for a lathe chuck.** "Add accessory…" shows a **Fit to the stock** checkbox for the 3-jaw, 4-jaw and collet chuck. Ticked, Place queues `InsertAccessory` with the existing `OnStock` placement; the grip diameter (or collet bore) is shown as "(set by the fit)" and disabled, and the pose rows give way to a line that says what the fit does. The box opens ticked when the setup's stock reads as round.
- **Inside grip** (`JawChuck::grip`, `outside` | `inside`). An inside jaw runs inward from the grip diameter; its gripping face is the arc of the bore it opens into, drawn circumscribed (flats on the grip circle, steps of at most 1/256 turn), so the drawn steel is never less than the jaw.
- **Stepped jaws** (`step_height`, `step_depth`; both 0 for plain jaws). Below the step height the jaw reaches the step depth past the gripping face, under the work. A stock fit seats the stock on the step: the chuck's face goes the step height below the stock's underside.
- **Refusals by name** (all in `camcraft_sim::chuck::jaw::check`): a step figure that is not finite, negative or over 5000 mm; one step figure without the other; a step as tall as its jaw; a step or an inside jaw that reaches the axis; steps or inside jaws that would meet each other; an inside jaw wider than its bore, shorter than its own arc, or past the body. A stock fit with an inside grip is refused ("an inside grip opens into the work's bore, which the stock's box does not give"); the dialog unticks and disables the box for an inside grip and says why.
- **MCP:** `add_accessory` and `set_accessory` take `grip`; the `dimensions` object takes `step_height` and `step_depth`; the result's `accessory` shows `grip` for a jaw chuck. The camcraft-mcp skill row now lists the three chuck kinds, `fit_to_stock`, `grip` and the step figures.
- **Files:** the three new fields are `serde(default)`, so a project saved before this reads as plain outside jaws, and the default chuck's mesh is unchanged to the triangle (pinned).
- Guide: `site/content/guide/set-up/workholding.md` describes the chuck rows. Decision record: `docs/decisions/1468-chuck-options.md`.

The jaw geometry lives in `crates/sim/src/chuck/jaw.rs` (new, with its provenance line); `chuck.rs` keeps the body, the collet and the round-stock read. No new crate dependency.

## Collision consequences (safety floor)

A generated chuck is an ordinary meshed fixture, so the new jaws reach the lathe holder law and the post gate through the same path as #1442:

- `inside_grip_jaws_are_steel_that_blocks_the_post`: a holder whose leg rides through inside-grip jaws is named and the post is blocked; the same holder 2 mm over the jaws posts.
- `stepped_jaws_are_steel_where_they_stand_under_the_work`: the same for stepped jaws with the face lowered by the step height.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green (sim, app and ui suites; 3 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Pinning tests:

- `crates/sim/tests/lathe_chuck_jaws.rs` (new): `outside_stepped_jaw_envelope_is_pinned`, `inside_grip_envelope_is_pinned`, `inside_stepped_jaw_envelope_is_pinned` (steel a hair inside every true face, air a hair past it, outward volume, the drawn arc never inside the true one), `step_nonsense_is_refused_by_name`, `inside_grip_nonsense_is_refused_by_name`, `a_file_from_before_reads_as_plain_outside_jaws`.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_chuck.rs`: the two collision tests above and `a_fit_seats_the_stock_on_the_step_and_refuses_an_inside_grip`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_accessory.rs`: `lathe_chucks_are_placed_fitted_to_the_stock_and_undone_over_mcp` (extended: `grip`, step figures, their refusals).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_accessory_tests.rs`: `chuck_dialog_offers_fit_to_the_stock`, `chuck_fit_is_off_by_pose_for_an_inside_grip_and_square_stock` (AccessKit labels, toggled and disabled state; no snapshot PNG changed).

## Not exercised

- The native GUI window was not launched. The visual evidence below uses the shipping shell and GPU viewport in an offscreen harness.
- Windows was not tested. Earlier validation ran on macOS. This evidence update uses Linux.
- Clicking **Inside** in the dialog leaves the generic figures as they are; for the generic 4-jaw (40 mm grip, 50 mm jaws) Place then refuses by name until the grip diameter is typed. No preset is offered for an inside grip.

## Visual evidence for review

Before: `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239` (the feature commit's parent). After: `a09aef1cd57e1c0abf1083595b27f66f2ec9fe6f`.

An offscreen egui harness captures the shell. The viewport uses GPU readback. The native GUI window was not launched.
The before images use the actual parent source. The after images use the reviewed head source.
No image or capture harness is committed to the PR branch.

title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

## UI before and after

These are headless captures of the real egui controls, rendered with `egui_kittest::Harness::render` on Linux. Before is pre-feature commit `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239`. After is reviewed head `af78aec60436e402c8e026d5bc9521552131bf5a`. The temporary harness called the shipping `cutting_rows` and `stock_page` functions; no UI was mocked. The cutting-data draft has the same Aluminium 6061 row in both captures. The after draft also states stepdown 2 mm and stepover 3 mm. The stock captures use the same seeded document.

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, at commit `b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d`. No capture harness, screenshot, golden, or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

| Control | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cutting data | ![Cutting data before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-before.png) | ![Cutting data after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-after.png) |
| Stock Material | ![Stock Material before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/stock-material-before.png) | ![Stock Material after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/stock-material-after.png) |

The after table shows the fixed Unknown row, the named material row, and the step fields. The after stock page shows the Material group between Shape and Size. Both render checks passed at each revision (four captures total). This was a headless UI render, not a manual native-window session.

## Not exercised

- No manual native-window UI session. The controls were rendered headlessly as shown above. The release-lane pixel snapshot comparisons were not run and no golden PNG changed.
- The camcraft-mcp skill row for `set_stock_material` is a follow-up (process-file change): #2076.
- A per-setup spindle speed (the S word by stock material) is out of scope: the tool's running rpm follows the document material.

Changelog: Tools keep cutting data per work material with an Unknown default row, an optional stepdown and stepover per row, and a setup stock may state its own material, which picks the row (stock, then document, then Unknown); older projects and tool libraries load unchanged (#2015)

Effort: high (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: project files are written as version 63 (and tool libraries with a stated Unknown row or steps as version 3); older builds refuse them.

Fixes #2015

title: fix(3d): assert band-edge levels and cross-band links in 3D Finish
body:
## What changed
Added a default-suite test (`the_3d_finish_band_split_levels_move_within_stepdown_and_links_cross_edge`) and helpers (`milling_test_finish_band`, `flat_feed_zs`) in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs`.
The test runs 3D Finish (`BN-0600`, kind defaults) on `Milling-test.step` across `[20.0, 18.0]`, `[18.0, 16.0]`, and the whole span `[20.0, 16.0]`.
It checks verification gates, zero gouge cells, band-edge Z shifts within `scallop_stepdown`, and the clearance `Rapid` + `Plunge` link across `edge_z = 18.0`.
Added `docs/decisions/1853-finish-band-edge-links.md`.

## Cause
PR #1846 split the heavy `sample_ap214.step` 3D Finish test into six Z bands.
That split pinned band boundaries to each band edge and left cross-band link generation and near-edge level shifts untested.
Production 3D Finish code already handles both; only the test was missing.

## Tests
- Pin: `the_3d_finish_band_split_levels_move_within_stepdown_and_links_cross_edge` in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` passes on `upstream/main` (`2 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored` in 6.75s) because #1853 only asks for the missing test.
- Temporary mutation 1 (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/ladder.rs` line 157, stepping by `1.5 * dz`, reverted): the pin failed (`z_above=18.838104996137776 stepdown=0.7745966692414834`) and passed again after restoring.
- Temporary mutation 2 (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/rings.rs` lines 414-420, dropping clearance `Rapid` retract/traverse between Z levels, reverted): the pin failed (`gouge: program cuts below the model in 9 cell(s), worst 0.19 mm at (0.44, -29.94, z 19.81)`) and passed again after restoring.
- Quick gate (`gate quick --base upstream/main`, run with `RUSTC_WRAPPER` unset and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` due to host `sccache` permission errors): green (`app suites`, `1 step(s), 0 failed`, 6s).
- Clippy (`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, run with `RUSTC_WRAPPER` unset): green (0 warnings).

## Goldens moved
None.

## Not exercised

body:
## What changed

- The three Tormach lathe files now state `"rigid_tapping": true`: `tormach-8l.mch`, `tormach-15l-slant-pro.mch` and `tormach-15lx-slant-pro.mch`.
- The pin now checks the lathes. Its new name is `every_tormach_mill_router_and_lathe_file_states_rigid_tapping`. It expects exactly three Tormach lathes. The plasma table stays outside the check.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` now says that the Tormach lathes state the key.
- `docs/decisions/795-lathe-rigid-tapping.md` cites the manuals.

## Cause

The lathe files did not state the key. The Machines pane read them as "not stated - not limited". The research comment on #795 found the answer in each operator manual:

- 8L: UM10753, section 10.3.18 "Rigid Tapping (G33.1)".
- 15L Slant-PRO: UM10225, section 6.5.17.
- 15LX Slant-PRO: UM10860, section 10.3.13.

## Tests

- Pin: `rigid_tapping::every_tormach_mill_router_and_lathe_file_states_rigid_tapping`.
- Red before the fix: `assertion left == right failed: Tormach 8L, left: None, right: Some(true)`.
- Mutations: I removed the key from each lathe file, one at a time. The pin failed each time and named the machine (`Tormach 8L`, `Tormach 15L Slant-PRO`, `Tormach 15LX Slant-PRO`). With the key restored, the pin passes.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): green. It ran `probe_no_coolant` and `rigid_tapping`.
- I also ran `machine_library`, `machine`, `posting` and `tormach_lathes`. All pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. Posted output does not change. The program gate refuses a tap only on a stated `false`. The post script default for `machine.rigidTapping` is already `true`. `tormach-lathe.cps` still refuses a `TAP` cycle by name.

## Not exercised

- No lathe tap output. G33.1 output in `tormach-lathe.cps` is later work. The decision file lists the rules from the manuals for that work.
- No check on a real PathPilot lathe control.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

Changelog: The Tormach 8L, 15L Slant-PRO and 15LX Slant-PRO machine files state rigid tapping (true, from their operator manuals); the Machines pane shows "yes" for them.

Fixes #795

title: fix(post): implement AC table-table inverse kinematics solver
body:
## What changed
Added the `camcraft_post::kinematics` module in `crates/post/src/kinematics/`.
Implemented `forward_machine` and `forward_part` using Rodrigues axis-angle rotation with configurable rotary axes, offsets, work datum, and rotary sign conventions.
Implemented `AcSolver` and `analytical_branches` to evaluate both `(+A, C)` and `(-A, C + 180 deg)` branches against `A.travel` and `C.travel`.
Added modal `C` holding inside `pole_sin_tol` near `A = 0` and weighted angular step minimization across branches for smooth zero crossings.
Added continuous `C` unwrapping inside sections, safe-retract re-wrapping, named refusals for invalid geometry or travel overflow, and quarter-point chord subdivision in `solve_path` and `solve_toolpath`.
Exported `kinematics` in `crates/post/src/lib.rs`, added tests in `crates/post/tests/ac_trunnion_ik.rs` and `crates/post/src/kinematics/tests.rs`, and recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/1965-ac-trunnion-ik.md`.

## Cause
The codebase lacked a shared pure-Rust XYZAC table-table inverse kinematics solver in `camcraft-post`, so machine checking and post processors had no common kinematic core for off-pivot offsets, rotary branch selection, pole holding, continuous C unwrapping, and chord subdivision.

## Tests
- Pins (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --test ac_trunnion_ik`): 7 passed (`round_trip_fk_ik_with_nonzero_offsets_within_micron`, `asymmetric_a_limits_select_reachable_branch_and_refuse_unreachable`, `pole_near_zero_holds_previous_modal_c_instead_of_snapping_to_zero`, `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip`, `continuous_c_unwrapping_and_safe_retract_rewrapping`, `subdivides_linear_moves_beyond_chord_tolerance_for_tip_accuracy`, `refuses_malformed_machine_geometry_and_non_finite_inputs`).
- Unit tests (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib kinematics`): 4 passed (`rollover_wraps_into_0_to_360_at_initial_and_safe_retract`, `positive_only_a_limits_reorient_c_at_pole_within_chord_tolerance`, `solve_toolpath_converts_cl_moves_and_detects_retract`, `refuses_non_positive_path_options_and_parallel_spindle`).
- Full crate suite (`cargo test -p camcraft-post`): all lib unit and integration suites passed before the final `solve.rs`/`travel.rs` extraction, and `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final tree.
- Mutation checks on `ac_trunnion_ik`:
  - Removed `pub mod kinematics;` in `crates/post/src/lib.rs`: failed compile -> restored -> passed.
  - Replaced modal `C` hold at pole with `0.0` in `solve.rs`: `pole_near_zero_holds_previous_modal_c_instead_of_snapping_to_zero` and `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip` failed -> restored -> passed.
  - Disabled weighted minimum-cost branch selection in `solve.rs`: `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip` failed (`dC=180`) -> restored -> passed.
  - Replaced strict `unwrap_near` + `C.travel` refusal in `Continuous` mode with re-wrap turn search in `solve.rs`: `continuous_c_unwrapping_and_safe_retract_rewrapping` failed -> restored -> passed.
  - Disabled `exceeds_chord_tol` check in `path.rs`: `subdivides_linear_moves_beyond_chord_tolerance_for_tip_accuracy` failed (`got 1` segment) -> restored -> passed.

## Goldens moved
None (`git diff --stat 17a8c6e7 -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised
Wiring `.mch` trunnion schema fields (#1962), `mach4.cps` posting (#1968), `G93` inverse-time feeds (#1966), and `machine::check_ops` integration (#1969) remain out of scope for those downstream issues.

## Overlaps
None on `crates/post/src/lib.rs`, `crates/post/src/kinematics/`, `crates/post/tests/ac_trunnion_ik.rs`, or `docs/decisions/1965-ac-trunnion-ik.md`.

Changelog: Added pure-Rust AC table-table forward/inverse kinematics solver and chord subdivider in `camcraft-post`.
Fixes #1965

title: fix(2d): clear Zigzag rest boundaries without wall cusps
body:
Stacked on #1817 (merge #1817 first)

## What changed

2D rest machining now accepts Zigzag. It cuts rows, then closes each rest boundary to clear wall cusps.

Rows use an inset of `min(0.01 mm, stepover / 4)`. This prevents numeric boundary crossings without removing interior rows from small pockets.

The existing plain-pocket row algorithm moves unchanged to `pocket_zigzag.rs`. `pocket.rs` stays at 398 lines. No dependency is added.

The MCP skill now describes Zigzag support. Adaptive still has its named refusal. The entered previous tool remains an explicit trust assumption.

The remaining #1490 work has separate issues: Adaptive #2031, entry from cleared space #2032, and previous-operation stock #2033.

## Cause

Rows alone leave cusps at the rest boundary. A closing pass clears them. Rows that touch the boundary can cross it through numeric rounding.

A fixed 0.01 mm inset removes all rows from a tiny pocket. The stepover cap preserves those rows.

The geometry follows this project's existing scan and offset routines. See Held's [Zigzag Pocket Machining](https://www.cosy.sbg.ac.at/~held/projects/pocket_zig/pocket.html) and [pocket geometry monograph](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9). [Yao, Gupta and Nau](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf) provide the cutter-coverage context. The inset and closing-pass choices are ours.

## Tests

- `zigzag_rest_covers_corner_residue_without_gouges_or_unsafe_rapids`: red at the original refusal. Green after the fix. Covers both directions and 1.5/4 mm steps.
- `tiny_rest_pocket_keeps_interior_rows_when_previous_tool_fits_nowhere`: red with the fixed inset. Green with the stepover cap.
- Expected-change tests now accept Zigzag at the motion and operation parameter doors.
- Closing-pass mutation: red coverage; restored green. The first fixture left 287 measured residue points uncut.
- Zero-inset mutation: red verifier, with six crossings; restored green.
- Fixed-inset mutation: red tiny-pocket center coverage; restored green.
- Old `upstream/main` pocket code: red; restored green.
- Old `base-1817` rest strategy: red refusal; restored green. The parent baseline supplies the export absent from `upstream/main`.

The requested `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all three steps in 34.4 minutes before the inset cap.

After the cap, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only motion` passed its affected motion step in 663 seconds.

Convert Gemini type arrays to anyOf and remove $schema from schema locations.
Preserve literal enum and default values.

Add call parsers and result adapters that preserve call IDs and MCP errors.
Validate tool names and arguments before returning a call.
Add local JSON proposals that require explicit confirmation for edits.
Add prompt context and read-only Q&A context for models without native tools.
The mapper prepares calls and does not execute them.

This branch starts at upstream/main cfc8447e.

title: fix(tools): preserve tap hand and refuse left-hand posting
body:
Stacked on #2001 (merge #2001 first)

## What changed

Store explicit tap hand on the tool.
Default older tools to right-hand.
Refuse malformed hand values by name.
Preserve hand through catalog import, tool JSON, project files, tool libraries, editor drafts and undoable commands.
Show the left-hand choice in the tap editor.
State that left-hand posting is unavailable.

Refuse left-hand taps in the shared posting preflight before records or NC files are emitted.
The refusal names the operation and tool.
It covers all eight built-in posts that implement tapping: Fanuc, Haas, Siemens 840D, Heidenhain, Mazak, Tormach PathPilot, Doosan DNM and Fanuc Lathe.
Right-hand output stays unchanged.

Write project version 62 for saved projects.
Use library version 2 only for exports containing a left-hand tap.
These versions make older readers refuse the files instead of silently losing hand.
Keep right-hand-only libraries at version 1.

## Cause

The tool model had no tap hand.
The tool JSON reader silently discarded an unknown hand field.
A left-hand declaration therefore could not survive the existing data path.
Every supported tapping cycle used the right-hand assumption.

Effort: high. No escalation.

## Tests

All 14 focused pins pass.
The first pin failed at runtime on unchanged product code.
It read `Null` instead of `left` after the JSON round trip.

App pins:

- `left_hand_tap_survives_tool_json_roundtrip`

- `every_tapping_post_refuses_left_hand_for_rigid_floating_and_auto`

- `tap_hand_checkbox_stages_until_apply_and_undo_restores_right`
- `a_non_tap_tool_has_no_tap_hand_checkbox`

All 11 mutation cases failed at runtime and passed after restoration:

- Restore the upstream posting preflight.
- Restore the upstream tool-library implementation.
- Accept an invalid hand as right-hand.
- Revert project version 62 to 61.
- Drop hand when writing the tool DTO.
- Drop hand when reading the tool DTO.
- Drop hand in catalog conversion.
- Refuse library version 2 in the new reader.
- Drop hand in `ToolUi::from_tool`.
- Drop hand in `ToolUi::to_tool`.
- Ignore the checkbox selection.

The posting and library replays restored whole files from `upstream/main`.
The new enum, DTO, catalog and UI mutations changed the relevant behavior in place.

It passed after restoration.
All mutations were restored.

All-targets clippy with `-D warnings` passed for `camcraft-app`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-post`.
The final Fanuc Lathe coverage required no product-code change.
All seven app pins and app all-targets clippy passed again after that test was added.

## Goldens moved

None.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

No physical control ran the output.
The full batch and release snapshot lanes were not run.
This change refuses left-hand posting; it does not implement left-hand controller cycles.

## Overlaps

#2001 changes shared conversion functions, including `ToolUi::from_tool`, the `ToolDto` conversions, the catalog definition conversion and `tool_editor_window`.
This branch started from #2001 at `028a0ad0` over upstream/main `cda3d589`.

- #1931, #1717 and #1209 each touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes. They share `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`.

title: fix(ui): prevent tool editor width growth from numeric overflow
body:
Stacked on #2001 (merge #2001 first)

## What changed

Keep oversized numeric controls aligned to the start of their allocated space.
The tool editor keeps its width across 100 frames with the pointer moving.
The fix changes `fields::num_sized` and preserves its width budgets and unit conversion.
The issue commit changes no tool editor column widths.
Record the decision in `docs/decisions/2003-tool-editor-width.md`.
Effort: low.

## Cause

The feed-rate `DragValue` exceeds the shared 96-point field budget when it draws `1800.0 mm/min`.
The old `ui.add_sized` centers the oversized control.
Its leading edge overflows by 1.8125 points.
That overflow feeds the next window layout and adds 1.8125 points per frame.
The existing tool editor grew from 770 to 951.25 points over 100 pointer frames.

## Tests

All four pins pass in the default UI value-test suite.

- `existing_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` failed before the fix.
- `new_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` covers the new-tool path and passes on both versions.
- `wide_metric_feed_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` covers a long metric feed.
- `wide_inch_feed_tool_editor_width_stays_put_after_100_pointer_frames` covers a long inch feed.

The mutation check copied the actual `upstream/main` version of `fields.rs` back into the worktree.
The existing-tool and both long-feed pins failed at runtime.
The wide metric case grew from 770 to 1314.8125 points.
The wide inch case grew from 770 to 1305.1563 points.
All four pins passed after restoring the fix.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all four steps with zero failures.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
The required gate also covers the inherited #2001 changes.

## Tool editor before and after pointer movement

These are 1280 × 720 headless renders of the shipping egui shell, captured with the existing-tool width-test setup and its 100 pointer-movement frames. The viewport is the harness placeholder. They are review evidence, separate from snapshot goldens.

The before renders use the original `num_sized` implementation from this issue commit's parent. The editor grows from 770 to 951.25 points. The after renders use this PR's fixed implementation. Its width stays at 770 points.

| Implementation | Initial frame | After 100 pointer frames |
|---|---|---|
| Before | ![Before: initial editor width 770 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/before-initial.png) | ![Before: editor width grows to 951.25 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/before-pointer100.png) |
| After | ![After: initial editor width 770 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/after-initial.png) | ![After: editor width stays at 770 points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55/2020/after-pointer100.png) |

The four PNGs are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch at `92400b9b58b87b08cfa9ba61d65ef63164d33d55`. Temporary capture code was removed. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Goldens moved

None.
The NC and CL golden diff against `upstream/main` is empty.

## Not exercised

No manual native-window session or release-lane pixel snapshot was run.
The other floating dialogs received a source audit.
The machine editor, G-code viewer, post refusal, and Debug info windows specify default sizes or widths.
The fixture library and unsaved prompt cap their content widths.
The G-code viewer also bounds its trace columns.
The audit found no reason to change those dialogs in this issue.

## Overlaps

#2001 changes `tool_editor_window`, which was the expected edit site during the overlap check.
This branch starts at its head `028a0ad0e`.
The final fix lives in `fields::num_sized` instead.
#2001 must merge first.

#1931 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
#1717 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
Both change WCS properties in `pages.rs`.
The `pages.rs` changes in this branch come unchanged from #2001.
The overlap check found no open PR touching `fields.rs` or `tests/tool_cutter.rs`.

title: fix(ui): replace the parameter holder with the tool body in preview
body:
## What changed

The editor uses the body bands for its holder when a body exists.
It removes the parameter holder from the fill, outline and frame calculation.
A tool without a body keeps its parameter profile.

## Cause

`draw_tool_preview` painted the full `Tool::profile()` and then painted the body over it.
Collision checking uses `tool_body::judged` and `tool_body::stack` to replace an explicit parameter holder with the body bands.
The viewport and simulation use those bands through `sim_tool_body::for_operation`.
The separate conservative parameter floor for assumed machine-default holders is tracked in #2009.
This PR changes editor paint only.

## Tests

- `tool_preview_body_replaces_parameter_holder_fill`
- `tool_preview_body_replaces_parameter_holder_outline`
- `tool_preview_body_sets_frame_without_parameter_holder`
- `tool_preview_without_body_keeps_parameter_holder`

The three body pins failed before the fix.
The no-body control passed.
The mutation restored upstream production code with identical test registration.
The three body pins failed again.
Restoring the fix passed all four tests.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed the UI library and boundary, boundary_picks, sinker_setup and theme_files suites.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

## Tool editor before and after

Both renders use the same tool and imported body: an Ø8 mm cutter, 20 mm flute,
40 mm shank, Ø60 × 60 mm parameter holder, and Ø24 × 20 mm body from z60 to z80.
These are headless renders of the actual tool editor at 1600 × 1400.
Before uses the parent preview function; after uses head `5e127955b69e032cfeac51f89d7a434b63b5ef8e`.

Before: the gray parameter holder overlaps the amber body and sets a 120 mm overall frame.

![Before: parameter holder overlaps tool body](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/05173e65caf23e7559f089362140f377c7e63598/2010/before.png)

After: the body replaces the parameter holder and sets an 80 mm overall frame.

![After: body replaces parameter holder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/05173e65caf23e7559f089362140f377c7e63598/2010/after.png)

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

## Goldens moved

None.
The NC and CL diff stat is empty.

## Not exercised

No manual desktop session or physical machining.
The machine-default conservative floor remains separate work in #2009.

## Overlaps

#2001, #1931 and #1717 touch `pages.rs`, different functions from `draw_tool_preview`; whichever merges second refreshes.
No stacked dependency.

Effort: medium.
Based on upstream/main cda3d5896, after v0.21.0.

Changelog: The tool editor preview shows a tool body in place of the overlapping parameter holder.

Fixes #2005

title: fix(ui): stand the work envelope on the table plane
body:
## What changed

The displayed mill envelope starts on the Z=0 table plane.
It keeps its full Z travel height.
X/Y keep the setup work origin as their reference.
Lathe cylinders keep their existing reference.
The tooltip states these references.
The decision record is in `docs/decisions/1963-envelope-table.md`.

## Cause

The viewport drew the program-space travel bounds directly.
Those bounds can extend below the table plane.
With `assets/machines/tormach-pcnc1100-s3.mch`, the fresh document implicit setup drew its bottom at Z=-419.1 mm.
X/Y have no equivalent height error against the table plane.
The current machine files do not state a table footprint for another X/Y reference.

No travel or reach check uses the drawn box.
`crates/post/src/machine/envelope.rs` supplies display data only.
The travel check in `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs` reads axis limits and program coordinates directly.
This fix changes no safety check.

## Viewport screenshots

Both images use the Tormach PCNC 1100 Series 3 machine file.
Both use a fresh document, the implicit setup, and the world origin.
The work envelope is visible in both images.
The GPU viewport and the application UI render at 1440 × 960 pixels.
The camera stays fixed: target [0, 0, 180] mm, yaw 0.9 rad, pitch 0.5 rad, distance 2400 mm.
A temporary test fixture captured the application UI and GPU viewport.
The fixture was removed after capture.

Before: the display shift is reverted. The box bottom is Z=-419.1 mm.

![Before: envelope below the table plane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2006/before.png)

After: the reviewed fix is restored. The box bottom is Z=0 mm.

![After: envelope starts at the table plane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2006/after.png)

The images are stored only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.
The PR branch contains no screenshot files.

## Tests

`mill_envelope_stands_on_table_for_all_travel_files` failed before the fix.
It checks each bundled box envelope with complete travel limits.
It pins the bottom at Z=0, the travel height, and the existing X/Y bounds.

`mill_envelope_stays_on_table_with_shifted_origin_and_inverted_z` failed before the fix.
It checks G54 at [10, 20, 70] mm with standard and inverted Z.

For mutation testing, I restored the original module from `upstream/main`.
Both pins failed again.
I restored the fix, and both pins passed.
All five envelope tests passed.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed.
It ran 817 unit tests and 25 integration tests.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

## Goldens moved

None.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

I did not run the native application or the pixel snapshot lane.
I did not run the release gate or physical machine motion.

## Overlaps

None found in the file overlap checks.

Changelog: Place the displayed mill work envelope on the table plane and preserve its travel height.

Effort: medium

Fixes #1963

title: fix(waterjet): add machine and nozzle kinds with validated cut data
body:
## What changed

Add the declared `waterjet` machine kind and `Waterjet` nozzle tool kind.
Require linear X/Y axes and allow optional Z.
Refuse spindle, live-tool, rotary, and milling-coolant keys by name.
Require zero nozzle RPM and positive finite kerf.
Store material/thickness recipes with cut feed, kerf, pierce time, abrasive delay, re-pierce time, and pierce method.
Check XY travel and feed limits, including arc extrema.
State which Z and spindle checks do not apply.
Preserve recipes through project files, tool libraries, and the tool editor.
Give the nozzle its own original icon.

The branch starts at upstream/main `cda3d5896` as requested.
The fork's main branch was not synced or changed.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/1881-waterjet-kinds.md`.
No dependencies or process files changed.
Effort: high.

The parser did not recognize waterjet machines.
The tool and cutting-row models had no waterjet kind or material/thickness recipe data.

title: feat(gate): one step for each test binary in quick, batch and release
body:
Process change: yes

What changed
- `cargo xtask gate quick`, `batch` and `release` plan one step for each test target of the debug suites, as the heavy lanes do (#1714). Step names: `<crate> suites: lib`, `bins`, `<binary>`, `doc`.
- Batch and release start with one build step (`cargo test --no-run`). Quick builds one time for each crate when the crate has more than one run step.
- Batch stops after a failed `debug build (--no-run)` step, as release does. A `--dry-run` does not read the checkout for each step (713 steps in about 1 s).
- Each step has its own log, time and pass or fail line. `--only "app suites: cmds"`, `--failed` and `--dry-run` work for one step.
- Batch keeps `lib` and the binaries, without `SLOW_BINARIES` (as before). Release adds `bins` and `doc`. The ui steps keep CWD `crates/ui`.
- The gate skill, the AGENTS.md tier table and the xtask usage text describe the new steps.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1941-gate-step-per-binary.md` (steps run in the same order as before; release keeps its waves; a step runs `cargo test -p x --test b`, no direct exe).

Plan sizes (`--dry-run`, this tree)
| Tier | Steps before | Steps after |
|---|---|---|
| batch | 10 | 713 |
| release | 189 | 911 |
| quick (for a diff) | one step for each crate | one step for each target, and a build step |

Measured (Windows, this machine)
- 7 geometry targets, build ready: one grouped cargo call 1.5 s. Seven steps through `cargo xtask gate batch --only "geometry suites"`: 5.0 s. So one cargo start is about 0.5 s. No step rebuilt anything (each ran in 0 s).
- Estimate, not measured: about 6 min more serial time in batch for 713 steps.
- Not measured: a full batch gate before and after (about 20 min each), and any Linux runner time. The release wave parallelism is unchanged.
- Follow-up #1951 (P7): run the exes from the cargo JSON paths to remove the cargo start.

Pinning tests (`cargo test -p xtask`, 142 pass)
- `step_tests::release_runs_every_target_of_every_crate_one_step_each`
- `step_tests::batch_runs_lib_and_each_non_slow_binary_one_step_each`
- `step_tests::only_and_failed_select_one_binary_step`
- `tests::heavy_fn_in_a_second_binary_keeps_the_build_step` (review fix: quick keeps the build step when a second binary has only heavy fns)
- `lanes_tests::release_executor_overlaps_lanes_and_keeps_failure_and_checkout_guards` (review fix: batch stops after a failed `debug build (--no-run)`)
- Updated: `tests::batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` and the quick plan tests.

Test count: no `#[test]` changed in the crates. The step targets of each crate equal the targets of `cargo test -p <crate>` (batch: minus `bins`, `doc` and the slow binaries, as before). The step tests pin this for every crate.

Real runs: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (xtask unit tests, green) and `cargo xtask gate batch --only "geometry suites"` (7 steps, green). Not run: a full batch or release gate; a quick gate over app or ui steps.

Changelog: Gate: quick, batch and release plan one step for each test binary, with its own log and time.
Effort: medium

Fixes #1941

title: fix(geometry): add bounded ASCII DXF reader
body:
## What changed

Add a bounded ASCII DXF reader in `camcraft-geometry`.
Read HEADER, TABLES, LAYER definitions, and basic planar entities.
Keep drawing units explicit and preserve exact lines, circles, arcs, and polyline bulges.
Keep layer names on primitives and count skipped annotations by kind.
Refuse malformed input and unsupported geometry by name.
Add no dependencies.

This branch starts at upstream/main `3580f388821d604e602728495a53df1881889b0d`, as requested for this issue.

## Cause

The geometry crate had no ASCII DXF reader.
Later profile-import work needs shared primitives, explicit units, and input limits.

## Tests

All 30 tests pass in `dxf` and `dxf_refusals`.
The initial tests failed to compile because unchanged upstream had no `dxf` module.
The layer-name limit also had a failing runtime pin before the guard was added.

Named pins include:

- `dxf_rectangle_keeps_layers_and_explicit_units`
- `dxf_missing_unitless_unknown_and_standard_scales_are_explicit`
- `dxf_circle_and_wrapping_arc_stay_exact`
- `dxf_bulge_sign_and_major_arcs_keep_the_exact_sweep`
- `dxf_legacy_polyline_uses_parent_layer_and_closing_bulge`
- `dxf_annotations_are_counted_by_kind`
- `dxf_layer_name_length_is_bounded_before_segment_copies`
- `dxf_declared_vertex_limit_is_checked_before_reading_vertices`
- `dxf_nonfinite_and_out_of_range_geometry_is_refused`
- `dxf_varying_z_within_and_between_entities_is_refused`
- `dxf_input_entity_and_vertex_caps_are_enforced`
- `dxf_deterministic_smoke_fuzz_never_panics`

Copying the actual upstream `lib.rs` back made both suites fail with the missing-module error.
Restoring the reader made both suites pass.

Runtime mutation checks ran 72 experiments.
Seventy experiments failed at runtime and passed after restoration.
Two individual changes remained unobservable:

- `units_missing_at_variable`: the final HEADER check still refuses the missing value.
- `missing_vertex_x`: callers only finish a pending vertex after X is present.

Removing both missing-unit checks failed a pin.
Replacing both pending-coordinate checks also failed a pin.
The missing-X check alone remains unobservable through the public API.
Every restoration passed. No mutation remains in the branch.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 10 steps.
The geometry change expanded the gate to batch. The run took 42.7 minutes and needed no reruns.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` also passed.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` has no output.

## Not exercised

This change adds the core reader. GUI import and downstream DXF machining workflows need later integration work.
Windows and macOS builds were not run.
Release-heavy tests and pixel snapshots were not run.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changed the planned files at the overlap check.

Changelog: Add a bounded ASCII DXF reader with explicit units, layers, exact planar primitives, and named input refusals.

title: fix(sim): preserve machined walls and cavities through side turns
body:
## What changed

Box stock with retained cut history now preserves machined walls and cavities through side-on quarter turns.
The carry retains swept-tool geometry and reads separate material intervals along the new columns.
Later cuts, stock clips, and further turns keep those intervals.
Fixture checks use the intervals on columns and between columns.
A fixture can contact a finished wall or occupy a cavity without a false collision.
The verdict still detects a later cut through the part.

The change starts from upstream/main `6f8b309d`.
Effort: max (not escalated).
No process files change.

## Cause

The old carry knew column heights but lost the wall position between column centres.
It extended a turned face to the next empty centre and filled cavities between the outer faces.
The pins reproduced a 6.5 mm wall instead of 6.2 mm.
The pocket floor became 6 mm instead of 2 mm.
A fixture in contact with the wall falsely penetrated it by 0.3 mm.

## Tests

All 40 targeted tests pass.
They cover the reported failures, all 16 side turns, translations, sub-cell cavities, later cuts, clips, tool profiles, and named refusals.
The three critical pins failed on unchanged product code before the fix:

- `a_contoured_wall_keeps_its_off_grid_position_after_a_side_turn`

title: fix(kernel): retry machining meshes at a finer chord
body:
## What changed

Retry a machining mesh once at half the planning chord when its measured deviation exceeds the requested tolerance.
Keep the existing minimum chord and all acceptance checks.
Record the finer chord in the mesh report.
The Solidcraft sample now meshes at the requested 0.005 mm tolerance.
Its measured deviation is 0.00323090453 mm, with all 53 faces and no open sides.

## Cause

The display planner measures normal distance at triangle midpoints and centroids.
The verifier uses denser samples and conservative parametric distance on rational-spline faces.
Nine sample faces exceeded the verifier's limit at the original planning chord.
Face 50 measured 0.00684674657 mm against the 0.005 mm limit.

## Tests

- `solidcraft_sample_meshes_within_the_app_chord` failed before the fix and passed after it.
- Restoring `upstream/main`'s production file made that pin fail again. Restoring the fix made it pass.
- `solidcraft_sample_still_refuses_an_out_of_tolerance_mesh` passed. At 0.1 mm, face 36 still exceeds tolerance after the retry.
- `a_bad_tolerance_or_a_spent_time_bound_is_refused_by_name` passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: one library test and seven machining-mesh tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- Targeted rustfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reported existing differences in unrelated files. No unrelated files were changed.

## Goldens moved

None. The `.nc` and `.cl` diff is empty.

The sampled deviation check does not prove the continuous closest-surface distance.

## What changed

This is slice 2 of issue 1473: item 3, a picked start point with tabs on a closed 2D Contour.

- `pick_ring` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs`) does not refuse tabs now. Control and wear compensation with a pick stay refused by name.

title: fix(post): refuse a bore dwell where G86 has no dwell word; pin G86 per post (#1445)
body:
## What changed

This is slice 2 of #1445: the boring cycle (G86: feed in, spindle stop, rapid out). The `Bore` cycle kind was already on main. This slice pins it per post and closes two dwell gaps.

- `assets/posts/{fanuc,haas,mazak,doosan-dnm,sinumerik}.cps`: a bore with a dwell is refused by name. Before this change, these posts wrote `P<ms>` on G86. The published Fanuc and Haas G86 formats have no P word, so the control dropped the dwell without a message. A bore with no dwell posts as before.
- tormach and grblhal keep `G86 ... P<seconds>` (the LinuxCNC G86 takes P as a dwell in seconds).
- The expanding posts (heidenhain, tinyg, carvera) do not change.
- New door `OpParams::dwell_refusal` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/dwell.rs`): a drilling dwell is a time from 0 to 3600 s (`MAX_DWELL_S`). `CreateOperation` and `EditOperationParams` refuse other values by name. MCP `edit_operation` uses the same command, so it refuses them too. The project loader does not use this door, so an old project still opens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1445-boring-g86.md`.

The default posted output does not change. No existing NC or CL golden changed.

## Sources

- NIST IR 6556 (The NIST RS274NGC Interpreter v3), G86.
- The LinuxCNC G-code reference (G86 with P in seconds).
- The public Fanuc 30i operator manual (B-63944EN) and the Haas mill programming workbook, for the G86 address words.

No vendor post file or CAM output was read.

- `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (7 tests): the stream round trip, G86 and no other cycle on the canned posts, the by-name dwell refusal on the Fanuc family and Sinumerik, `P0.5` on tormach and grblhal, the expanded chain with its dwell, the refusal on posts without drilling, and new goldens in `crates/post/tests/golden/bore/` (fanuc, haas, heidenhain, sinumerik, grblhal, tormach).

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket operation
body:
Fork synced at v0.20.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71).

## What changed

The 2D Pocket can now cut only what a larger previous tool left. It uses the rest generator of #1446 (`machining2d::rest_pocket`).

- **Parameter.** `OpParams::Pocket` has a new optional `rest` group: previous tool diameter, its corner radius, the stock it left on the walls, and the rest allowance. `None` is off. Off is the default and the plain pocket.
- **Undoable edit.** You change the group through `EditOperationParams`. Undo and redo restore it.
- **Project file.** The key is `rest` (an object). A file without the key reads as off, so the file version does not change.
- **Stamp.** The stamp writes the group (byte `0xD7`) only when it is on. Each value of the group changes the stamp.
- **Generation.** When the group is on, generation calls `rest_pocket`. Its note ("rest machining trusts the entered previous tool ...") goes into the path notes.
- **Refusals by name, in the generator's own words, when you make, edit or retool the operation** (not only at Generate):
  - a previous tool that is not larger than the operation's tool (new `rest_gate`, run from `tool_gate` and from the edit);
  - a value that is negative or not finite, a previous tool diameter that is 0 or less, or a corner radius larger than the previous tool's radius;
  - the Zigzag or Adaptive strategy;
  - pre-drilled entry with rest machining on (`REST_PREDRILLED`). `rest_pocket` does not read the holes, and the program must not drop a user setting without saying so.
- **Motion crate.** `RestParams` has a new `validate_alone` (the checks that do not need a tool, plus "the previous tool diameter must be positive"). The strategy check moved into a public `rest_strategy`. Its text did not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` sets the group (`"rest": null` turns it off). There is a new row in the camcraft-mcp skill. Area: mcp.
- **Not in this PR: the dialog group.** It is not part of "Done means", and it needs before/after screenshots and the UI gate. The page keeps the group as it is when you apply the page. Follow-up: #1815.

## How tested

The new pinning tests are in `crates/app/tests/rest_pocket.rs`:
- `the_rest_pass_cuts_only_the_corners_posts_and_matches_its_golden`: the fixture is a 60 x 40 pocket with 3 mm corners. A 12 mm end mill roughs it, then a 4 mm end mill does the rest pass. The golden is `pocket_rest_corners.cl`. All cuts stay in the corners. The program posts and the verification report is clean.
- `read_against_the_simulated_roughing_pass`: the roughing pass is simulated first on the stock dexel grid. Then:
  - no rapid of the rest pass hits stock;
  - every plunge goes down on floor that is already clear, and its rim touches stock for no more than one level;
  - all 8 rings (4 corners x 2 levels) cut stock, and air is less than half of each ring.
- `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_and_the_project_file_keeps_it`
- `a_previous_tool_that_is_not_larger_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_the_retool` (edit, create and retool)
- `values_and_strategies_the_rest_pass_cannot_run_are_refused_by_name`
- `mcp_sets_refuses_undoes_and_saves_the_group` (set, refuse, save, reopen, null, undo)

Other tests:
- `operation::rest_op_tests::the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`
- `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs`: a new case for a 0 mm previous tool.

Mutation check: I deleted each new refusal line, the stamp line and the generation line one at a time, ran the test that pins it, and saw it fail. Then I restored the file and compared it with a backup. All 11 failed when deleted and were restored byte for byte: the motion "must be positive" check, rest_op's three refusals, sane's `named_refusal` and `is_sane` lines, `rest_gate` in `tool_gate`, `rest_gate` in the edit, the refusal arm inside `rest_gate`, the `0xD7` stamp block, and the `rest_pocket` call in generation.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick` plans almost the whole workspace for this diff, so I ran the touched suites by name instead (motion: lib, rest2d, machining2d, predrilled_entry, corner_arc_radius, optimal_load, solid_law; app: lib, rest_pocket, golden_cl, arc_turn_params, predrilled_entry, project_roundtrip, roughing2d, adaptive_trochoid, mcp, mcp_pockets, pocket_recognition, operations, commands_undo, tool_gate, tool_law, verify, solid_law_goldens, heights, tilt, corner_blend, climb_direction, area_controls, pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, units_in_refusals, lead_approach, level_links, whole_model_pocket, recorded_post_streams; ui: lib, edge_loop_pick, operations). All green. Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion, camcraft-app and camcraft-ui (all targets): clean.

The existing pocket goldens do not change (`golden_cl`, `adaptive_trochoid`, `roughing2d` and the others in the list above).

## What I did not test

- I did not run the program on a machine, and I did not take screenshots (there is no UI change).
- Two things I measured but did not fix, because they are generator behaviour and not part of this slice:
  - The inner leg of each corner ring crosses floor that the 12 mm tool already cleared: 6.7 mm of a 14.8-15.3 mm ring. Follow-up: #1816.
  - On each level, 2 of the 4 corner plunges touch rest material at the rim. The tool axis is over cleared floor. Entry from cleared space belongs to #1490.
- All of these are feed moves, so they cost time, not safety.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1489-rest-pocket-param.md`.

Changelog: 2D Pocket rest machining: cut only what a larger previous tool left (previous tool entered by hand); undoable, saved in the project, set through MCP; a previous tool that is not larger is refused by name (#1489)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1489

title: fix(ui): offer stock fitting only for parametric shapes
body:
What changed: Hide Fit margin and Fit to Models for From model stock. Clear stale setup feedback when the draft shape changes. Keep Delete routed to deletion.

Cause: The page offered fitting for every stock shape. Its action routing depended on button positions. Shape changes kept feedback from the old draft.

Tests: stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape and stock_shape_change_clears_the_fit_refusal pass after merging upstream/main. The earlier run recorded both pins red before the fix. Restoring the old page and removing each guard made the pins fail again. The quick gate and UI clippy with warnings denied pass.

Goldens moved: None.

Not exercised: Native interactive UI.

Overlaps: The merge had one conflict in the test module list. Both sides remain.

Changelog: Hide unsupported stock fit controls for From model stock and clear stale fit refusals when its shape changes.

Fixes #1683

## Screenshots

The UI test harness renders these views at 1280×720 in the default dark theme. The viewport uses the harness placeholder.
Both columns use the merged UI harness and layout. Before substitutes upstream/main's Stock page (`a49322b9c`). After uses the merged PR source (`589d0f855`).

Box keeps the Fit margin group and the Fit to Models button.

title: fix(ui): turn WCS about its own axes
body:
What changed: WCS Turn X/Y/Z buttons rotate about the setup's current axes. The page now names the setup axes.

Cause: The quarter turn was left-composed with the orientation, so it acted in the world frame. Right composition applies it in the setup frame.

Tests: `quarter_turns_follow_each_oblique_setup_axis_in_both_directions` pins all three axes and both signs on an oblique setup and preserves the origin. The earlier run recorded that this pin failed before the fix. Its mutation restoring the old composition failed; restoring the fix passed. The publication run rechecked the pin, quick gate, and camcraft-ui all-targets clippy.

Goldens moved: None. No NC or CL goldens changed.

Not exercised: Interactive GUI clicks and physical machining.

Overlaps: Changes are limited to the WCS page, its tests, and the issue decision file. No stacked dependency. Fork synced at v0.19.0; this branch also includes current upstream/main.

Changelog: WCS quarter turns now rotate about the setup's own axes.

Fixes #1495


## Screenshots

Rendered off-screen with the UI test harness in the default dark theme at 1280×800. Before is upstream/main; After is this PR's head. The ribbon/browser styling also differs because upstream/main has newer unrelated UI changes.

The same oblique setup starts at roll 23°, pitch −31°, yaw 47°; look at the quarter-turn hint changing from world axes to setup axes.

title: fix(post): state the stock's turning radius on lathe streams
body:
Stacked on #1667 (the G30 logic of the Tormach lathe post). The diff shows the commits of #1667 until #1667 merges.

## What changed

- `Dump` in `camcraft-post` gets the field `stock_turn_radius`. When it is set, finite and more than 0, the stream gets `PARAM StockTurnRadius` after `StockZTop`.
- The new module `crates/app/src/stock_turn.rs` calculates the radius: the largest distance of a stock mesh vertex from the spindle axis (the world Z line through the setup origin).
- `posting.rs` sets the radius only for a lathe or mill-turn setup. Mill streams do not change.
- `tormach-lathe.cps`: `stockEnv()` uses the larger of the box half-width and `StockTurnRadius`. Thus the G30 approach and departure clear the rotating corners of a square bar.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` does not read the stock. It does not change.
- `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` gets a row for the new property.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/1666-stock-turn-radius.md`.

## Posted G-code changes

Yes, for a lathe program on a box (square bar) stock with the Tormach lathe post. The G30 departure goes to the corner diameter, not to the box width. A round bar gives the same radius as before, so its output does not change. No real control ran the output.

## Golden question (held for the maintainer)

Two goldens are stale on this branch. I did not regenerate them:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/axial_drill_mm.nc`: the last `G0 X24` becomes `G0 X33.941`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/axial_drill_inch.nc`: the same move in inch (`X0.9449` becomes about `X1.3363`).

The fixture uses a 24 x 24 box stock. The corners of the box turn on a circle of radius 16.971 mm (diameter 33.941). The new value is the correct clearance. Thus `lathe_post_tormach::an_axial_drill_posts_as_plain_moves_in_mm_and_inch` fails until the maintainer accepts the golden change.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_turn_radius.rs`:

- `a_lathe_stream_states_the_radius_its_stock_sweeps`
- `a_mill_stream_states_no_turning_radius`
- `the_g30_moves_use_the_square_bars_corner_circle`
- `a_square_bar_program_has_no_g30_rapid_inside_the_corners_circle`

All four pass. These suites also pass: `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach_g30`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_workholding_mill_post`, `solid_law_goldens`, `tormach_lathes`, `turning_stock_approach` (camcraft-app), and `recorded_streams`, `post_engine`, `lathe_post_refusals` (camcraft-post). `lathe_post_tormach` has 7 of 8 pass; the failure is the golden above. Clippy on `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-post` (all targets) is clean.

Not exercised: the full quick gate, a real PathPilot control, mill-turn posts, and the UI.

Changelog: The Tormach lathe post now clears the corners of a square-bar stock in its G30 approach and departure moves (the stream states StockTurnRadius).

Effort: high (no escalation).

Refs #1666

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
The stack parents #517 (#417) and #518 (#418) are merged. The diff now holds only the #419 work.

## Merge-time refresh (maintainer's session, head 39632f647)
The maintainer's session took this PR over for a merge-time refresh. It merged `origin/main` (62e1d36a6) into the branch. It did not rebase or force-push.

Hand-resolved hunks (keep both sides):
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `threadHalfTurn`: the PR's dip chain is kept. Main changed the lead word from `fr()` to `fl()` (#902: an inch lead has six decimals). Both G32 blocks of the chain (the plain block and the dip block `G32 X Z F`) now use `fl()`. The three refusals of the chain (no open chain, steeper than 45 degrees, deeper than the pass) are kept.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, manifest: `continuousThreading = true` with its citation, and main's `workOffsetIndex`, `workOffsetMax`, `explainWords`, `explainTool`, `programUnits`, `explains`, `commentMax`, `explainBlockMax`.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, G76 header comment: the PR's chip-break dips clause and main's `g76Allowance` paragraph (#517). `g76Why` keeps the two refusals: `RepeatEachDepth` (#518) and `ChipBreakDips`.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: main's manifest list with `continuousThreading` added ("the last nine").
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`: the `ChipBreakDips` refusal and main's `MillSpindle` reverse refusal (#988).
- `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`: the `continuous_threading` and `mill_spindle_reverse` fields.

No refusal of #517, #518 or main is lost. The Tormach lathe post does not declare `continuousThreading`, so the engine refuses dips on it by name. Its G76 `RepeatEachDepth` refusal (#518) is unchanged. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only the 26 files of this PR.

Readings after the refresh (`cargo test -j 6 -p <crate> --test <binary>`, one binary at a time):
- camcraft-motion: `turning_thread_dips` 9/9, `turning_thread_cycle` 3/3, `turning_thread_infeed` 10/10, lib 366 passed (5 ignored).
- camcraft-post: `inverted_post` 16/16, `recorded_streams` 12/12, lib 54/54.
- camcraft-cl: lib 41/41.
- camcraft-app: `lathe_post_thread_dips` 6/6 (golden `thread_g32_dips.nc` unchanged), `lathe_post_g76` 8/8, `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 7/7, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` 8/8, `lathe_post_css` 10/10, `turning_thread` 10/10, `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5, `lathe_thread_travel` 2/2, `conformance` 7/7, `coarse_laws` 6/6, `lathe_field_tools` 2/2, `project_roundtrip` 73/73.
- camcraft-ui: lib filter `thread` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised by the refresh: an inch program with dips (the `fl()` lead word under G20 has no golden), and a run on a controller or a simulator.

MCP: the dips ride the generic `edit_operation` tool through the project params JSON (`ThreadInfeedDto.dips`). No new MCP tool is necessary.

Screenshots: before and after screenshots on the refreshed head are in the section "Screenshots (Passes tab)" below.

Note: `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs` (600 lines) and `js.rs` (529 lines) were already more than 400 lines on main. This PR adds 4 and 17 lines to them.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Changelog: Threading: optional in-pass chip-break dips on roughing passes, posted as continuous G32 X Z F segments by the Fanuc lathe post (#419)

Fixes #419

## Screenshots (Passes tab)

Headless render (egui_kittest Harness::render()) of the Threading Passes tab, on the refreshed head 39632f647. Before is origin/main. The page header still reads "Contour1": the harness retypes the draft of the seeded operation, not the operation itself. Dip height and Dip length show only when Chip-break every is not 0. The after image uses Chip-break every 3.0 mm, Dip height 0.2 mm and Dip length 1.0 mm.

Before (origin/main): the Passes tab ends with Repeat each depth and Hand. No dip rows.

![before](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/65e120d963438e7a2bbc1873e623da182637a2c4/pr-468/before.png?raw=true)

After (this PR): the rows Chip-break every, Dip height and Dip length sit between Repeat each depth and Hand.

![after](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/65e120d963438e7a2bbc1873e623da182637a2c4/pr-468/after.png?raw=true)
